items.abstract: Menopause represents a physiologic transition characterized by the cessation of ovarian follicular estrogen synthesis and subsequent alterations in the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, with broad systemic and cutaneous consequences. This review (Part 1) provides a comprehensive overview of the epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and clinical evaluation of dermatologic manifestations associated with perimenopause and menopause. We summarize key hormonal changes, including declining estrogen and dynamic androgen shifts, and their downstream effects on skin structure and function through nuclear and membrane-associated estrogen receptor signaling pathways. The impact of estrogen deficiency across major cutaneous compartments-including the epidermis, dermis, hair follicle unit, sebaceous glands, vasculature, pigmentary system, and immune milieu-is examined, with emphasis on mechanisms underlying xerosis, impaired barrier function, dermal atrophy, alopecia, vasomotor instability, dyschromia, delayed wound healing, and vulvovaginal dermatoses. Dermatology-specific examination findings, limited utility of routine hormonal testing, and specific laboratory workup in patients with atypical or rapid-onset cutaneous hyperandrogenism are covered. This review equips clinicians with a mechanistic understanding of menopause-associated skin changes to support accurate diagnosis, appropriate workup, and informed management.

items.title: Surgical Management of Thoracic Aortic Mural Thrombus: Operative Strategy and Early Outcomes in a Two-Decade Retrospective Single-Center Experience.

sections.objective: Thoracic aortic mural thrombus (TAMT) is a rare but life-threatening condition due to the risk of systemic embolization. In this single-center retrospective surgical case series, we evaluated perioperative management, operative strategy and outcomes after surgical thrombectomy for TAMT, a condition with limited evidence and no established treatment standard.
sections.methods: Between 2004 and 2025, 14 patients (median age 57.5 years; 9 male) underwent open thrombectomy for TAMT at our institution. TAMT was defined as an intraluminal, imaging-confirmed thrombus attached to a non-aneurysmal and non-dissected aortic wall without identifiable cardiac or proximal embolic source.
sections.results: Acute systemic embolization represented the first clinical manifestation in the majority of patients, including stroke (n = 6), limb ischemia (n = 6) and visceral ischemia (n = 2). Thrombus localization included the ascending aorta (n=1), aortic arch (n=6), combined ascending aorta and arch (n=5), arch and descending thoracic aorta (n=1), and multiple thoracic aortic levels (n=1). All procedures were performed under cardiopulmonary bypass and hypothermic circulatory arrest allowing complete thrombus removal in all patients. One patient died within 30 days in hospital due to sepsis. Two disabling postoperative strokes and one new postoperative peripheral embolic event occurred. Median follow-up time was 3.5 months (IQR 0.4-60.7). No persistent or recurrent TAMT was observed during imaging follow-up (median imaging follow up 0.6 months).
sections.conclusion: Open surgical thrombectomy with hypothermic circulatory arrest permitted complete macroscopic thrombus removal in this selected surgical cohort and was technically feasible.

items.title: Empirical tuberculosis treatment in infants living with HIV hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa (EMPIRICAL): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, 2 × 2 factorial, controlled superiority trial.

sections.objective: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high globally. The EMPIRICAL trial evaluated whether empirical tuberculosis treatment (eTB-T) improves survival compared with the currently recommended microbiologically and clinically guided strategy.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2×2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia, without a current tuberculosis diagnosis or contact, were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity. A computer-generated block randomisation schedule was used, with fixed blocks of eight allocations (two allocations to each factorial treatment group) within each stratum. Participants received standard of care (SoC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SoC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. Here, we report the comparison between the eTB-T (ie, SoC plus tuberculosis treatment and SoC plus oral valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and non-eTB-T (ie, SoC or SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir) groups. Nasopharyngeal aspirates, stools for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing, and urine for tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay were collected at recruitment. In the non-eTB-T groups, tuberculosis treatment was initiated if microbiological results collected at recruitment yielded positive results or if, during follow-up, the treating clinician suspected tuberculosis on clinical grounds, including radiological findings, in accordance with routine clinical practice and guidelines. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality (at 15 days and 360 days). Survival was estimated using flexible parametric models with covariate-adjusted conditional estimates; missing data were imputed by chained equations. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03915366) and is now complete.
sections.results: Between March 15, 2020, and Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were analysed after excluding five patients who did not meet eligibility criteria. 276 participants were allocated to the eTB-T groups (n=140 eTB-T and n=136 valganciclovir plus eTB-T) and 282 to the non-eTB-T groups (n=142 SoC and n=140 valganciclovir). 17 (6%) of 276 in the eTB-T groups and 20 (7%) of 282 in the non-eTB-T groups were lost to follow-up. Median age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4) and 274 (49%) of participants were female and 284 (51%) were male. In the non-eTB-T groups, 130 (46%) of 282 participants eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment at a median of 4·0 days (IQR 3·0-15·0) after recruitment due to positive microbiological findings in 55 (20%) cases (53 confirmed by tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay and two by nasopharyngeal aspirates Xpert MTB/RIF) or clinical decision in 75 (27%) cases. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and eTB-T (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19, 95% CI 0·73-1·95; pheterogeneity=0·4836). At 12 months, 132 (48%) of 276 participants in eTB-T groups and 121 (43%) of 282 participants in non-eTB-T groups died. In the eTB-T groups, the adjusted hazard ratio for death was 1·12 (95% CI 0·87-1·43; p=0·3868). At 15 days, the odds ratio was 1·24 (95% CI 0·83-1·84; p=0·2950). Serious adverse events did not differ between groups (1·19, 0·82-1·73; p=0·3523). There were no treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events were elevation of transaminases (72 [26%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 74 [26%] in the non-eTB-T group), anaemia (163 [59%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 169 [60%] in the non-eTB-T groups), and infectious disease requiring antimicrobial treatment (161 [58%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 176 [62%] in the non-eTB-T groups).
sections.conclusion: In contrast to empirical treatment with valganciclovir, there was no evidence that eTB-T was superior to a clinically and microbiologically guided strategy in reducing all-cause mortality among infants with HIV-associated pneumonia. However, the high proportion of infants who eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment during follow-up in the non-eTB-T groups might have reduced the contrast between strategies and attenuated the ability to detect differences in outcomes.

items.title: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.
sections.methods: The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71 [49%]), nausea (seven [5%], 41 [28%]), decreased neutrophil count (five [3%], 40 [28%]), peripheral neuropathy (none, 38 [26%]), and fatigue (20 [13%], 37 [26%]). Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14 (9%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 21 (15%) of 144 participants in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group; they resulted in death in two participants in the pembrolizumab group (hepatic failure and bacterial meningitis [n=1 each]) and one participant in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (pulmonary embolism).
sections.conclusion: First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).

items.title: 14-day versus 28-day trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan.

sections.objective: Trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) plus bevacizumab is the standard treatment for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. However, the conventional schedule is frequently associated with haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, which is clinically significant and relevant to patients. A simplified 14-day schedule has been proposed to reduce toxicity, but whether this treatment preserves survival has not been established in a randomised trial. We therefore aimed to assess whether the 14-day schedule is non-inferior to the conventional schedule for overall survival.
sections.methods: PRABITAS was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial conducted in 178 hospitals in Japan. Patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) using a minimisation algorithm, stratified by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, RAS mutational status, and institution, to FTD-TPI (35 mg/m2 orally twice daily) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg intravenously) on either a conventional 28-day (FTD-TPI on days 1-5 and 8-12; bevacizumab on days 1 and 15) or 14-day schedule (FTD-TPI on days 1-5; bevacizumab on day 1). Eligibility criteria were broadened compared with those of conventional explanatory trials, and trial procedures were aligned with routine clinical practice. The primary endpoint was overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 1·25. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose. Missing data were not imputed. This trial is registered with the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials, jRCTs041230120, and is closed to enrolment.
sections.results: Between Dec 26, 2023, and May 20, 2025, we randomly assigned 972 patients, of whom 970 (99%) constituted the intention-to-treat population after two were excluded because they were randomly assigned before site approval (486 [50%] to the 28-day treatment group, 292 [60%] men and 194 [40%] women]; and 484 [50%] to the 14-day treatment group, 264 [55%] men and 220 [45%] women). Median follow-up was 17·9 months (IQR 14·3-22·6). Median overall survival was 10·3 months (95% CI 9·5-11·6) in the 28-day group and 11·3 months (10·2-12·5) in the 14-day group (stratified hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·80-1·08]). The 12-month overall survival rates were 44·0% (95% CI 39·5-48·5) in the 28-day group and 47·5% (42·9-52·0) in the 14-day group. Neutropenia grade 3 or worse was reduced in the 14-day group (13% vs 39%; absolute difference 25 percentage points [95% CI 20-31]), as was anorexia grade 2 or worse (15% vs 26%; absolute difference 11 percentage points [6-16]). Two treatment-related deaths occurred in the 14-day group and none in the 28-day group.
sections.conclusion: A 14-day schedule of FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

items.title: Ambient scribes as narrative technologies.
items.abstract: Ambient scribes, also known as artificial intelligence-powered voice-to-text technology, are widely cited as time-saving tools that reduce administrative burden for clinicians. Yet, in their current use, these tools pose substantial, often unacknowledged risks that threaten to undermine patient-centred care. We argue that ambient scribes are inherently narrative technologies whose risks-and potential benefits-cannot be fully understood without careful attention to the ways that patients tell their stories and the broader context in which those stories are told. Drawing on medical humanities scholarship, we show that current approaches to ambient scribes take a superficial approach to narrative interpretation that omits the clinically relevant aspects of patient experience. We propose three ways to integrate more robust narrative analysis that can increase the value of ambient scribes: centring patient perspectives, accounting for material and social structures that shape narrative, and reframing the clinical encounter as a node in a broader narrative system. We conclude by outlining five priorities for commissioners, administrators, clinical leaders, and practice managers to ensure that the roll-out of ambient scribes does not deepen existing harms, and could instead contribute to more humane and trustworthy care.

items.title: Empirical treatment with valganciclovir in infants living with HIV and hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa: a multicentre, open-label, factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.

sections.objective: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high. This trial (EMPIRICAL) tested whether empirical valganciclovir treatment for cytomegalovirus improves survival in infants in Africa.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2 × 2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity to receive standard of care (SOC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SOC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SOC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, assessed at day 15 and over 1-year follow-up in the intention-to-treat population. In this Article, we report results for the valganciclovir comparison groups. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03915366 and is complete.
sections.results: From March 15, 2020, to Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were included in the analyses, with 276 allocated to valganciclovir groups (140 valganciclovir; 136 valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and 282 to groups without valganciclovir (142 SOC; 140 tuberculosis treatment). The median patient age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4), and 274 (49%) were female. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and tuberculosis treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19 [95% CI 0·73-1·95], heterogeneity p=0·48). At day 15, 64 (23%) of 276 participants in the valganciclovir group and 76 (27%) of 282 in groups without valganciclovir died (rate ratio 0·81 [95% CI 0·61-1·08], p=0·15). 24 (9%) of 276 participants and 13 (5%) of 282, respectively, were lost to follow-up. After 12 months, 119 (43%) of 276 participants in the valganciclovir groups and 134 (48%) of 282 in the groups without valganciclovir died (0·88 [95% CI 0·74-1·05] p=0·15). In a time-varying effects model, at day 15, the adjusted hazard ratio of death was 0·60 (95% CI 0·41-0·87, p=0·0063), and their hazard of death over 1 year was 0·79 (0·62-1·01; p=0·068), or 0·76 (0·58-1·00; p=0·0500) when excluding deaths within 48 h of treatment. Severe adverse events during follow-up were not more common in the valganciclovir treatment groups (odds ratio 0·64 [95% CI 0·35-1·16]).
sections.conclusion: Empirical valganciclovir treatment appeared to be associated with a lower hazard of death in infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia than SOC alone or SOC plus empirical tuberculosis treatment, and there was little evidence of associated harms.

items.title: Impact of True and False Lumen Origins on Target Vessel Instability in Post-Dissection F/BEVAR.

sections.objective: To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen.
sections.methods: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI). Secondary endpoints included 5-year primary patency, freedom from secondary interventions (SIs), and type Ic and IIIc endoleaks. The analysis was performed on a per-vessel basis.
sections.results: A total of 1052 target arteries were analyzed, primarily including the celiac, superior mesenteric, and renal arteries, with individual hepatic and splenic arteries occasionally incorporated in the repair. Of the 277 patients included, 75% were men, and 19% were black, with a mean age of 66.8 ± 10.3 years. The mean aneurysm sac diameter was 66.0 ± 11.4 mm, with extent II thoracoabdominal aneurysms being the most prevalent (72.6%) among this cohort. Technical success was obtained in 96% of the cases. As primary outcome, the incidence of target vessel instability (TVI) was significantly lower (P<0.001) among the true-lumen vessels (16.4%) compared to false-lumen (29.9%) and dual-lumen arteries (43.8%). As for the secondary outcomes, the incidence of type Ic endoleak was significantly higher (P=0.001) in false-lumen vessels (9.6%) and dual-lumen vessels (8.6%) compared to true-lumen vessels (3.3%). There was no significant difference in the incidence of type IIIc endoleak (p=0.241) or target vessel occlusion (P=0.458). Target artery stenosis was significantly more common among arteries originating from the false lumen compared to true lumen (2.6% vs 0.4%, P=0.009). Fenestrations were associated with a higher incidence (30.5%) of TVI when compared to branches (5.9% P=0.005), however, this was observed only among dual-lumen vessels. Arteries incorporated by a fenestration and that had a dual-lumen origin, were associated with a higher occurrence of secondary interventions (23.7%) compared to true-lumen vessels (8.6%, P=0.010). The same was not observed among the arteries incorporated by a branch configuration. The time-to-event analysis demonstrated a significantly higher 5-year freedom from TVI in true-lumen vessels compared to false and dual-lumen ones (True lumen: 83.6%; False=70.1 %; Dual=56.2 %; Log-rank P=0.0002). Freedom from secondary interventions at 5 years was significantly higher in true-lumen vessels compared to dual-lumen ones (Log-rank P=0.0104), but not to false-lumen arteries (Log-rank P=0.0847). The 5-year primary patency did not differ significantly among groups (True lumen: 98.3%; False = 92.6%; Dual=93.9%; Log-rank P=0.1368). On Cox proportional hazards analysis, dual-lumen (95% CI 1.24-3.28, p=0.005) and false-lumen (95% CI 1.04 - 2.60, p=0.0325) target arteries were associated with an increased hazard of TVI, when compared to true lumen arteries, having 2.02 (P=0.005) and 1.65 (P=0.0325) times more risk of presenting TVI than a true-lumen vessel CONCLUSIONS: In F/BEVAR for post-dissection aneurysms, target vessel instability and secondary intervention are significantly lower in target arteries originating from the true lumen, when compared to false-lumen or dual-lumen vessels. Device design, with use of fenestrations or branches may also play a role, with a significant difference only observed in dual-lumen target arteries.

items.title: Fenestrated Endografts Provide Superior Outcomes Compared to Branched Devices in Juxtarenal Aortic Repair.

sections.objective: Urgent endovascular juxtarenal aortic repair with custom-made fenestrated devices is not feasible due to its long elaboration time. Off-the-shelf branched devices can be used, however, durability of the target vessels, especially renal artery branches, is of concern. Our objective is to compare mid and long-term patency of target vessels (TV), especially renal arteries (RA) in juxtarenal fenestrated or branched aortic endovascular repair.
sections.methods: Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing fenestrated or branched endovascular repair (f/bEVAR) for juxtarenal aortic aneurysms (JAA) between 2011-2022. A FEVAR group with use of fenestrations to incorporate target vessels (TV) and a BEVAR group, with use of branches were created. Clinical and anatomical characteristics as well as perioperative technical success and complications were compared. The primary endpoint was the assessment of RA primary patency, freedom from endoleaks and instability (endpoint including occlusion, endoleak or need for reintervention) at follow-up. Secondary endpoints were the assessment of CT-SMA patency rates, freedom from endoleak and instability at follow-up and the evaluation of the anatomical and clinical factors associated with renal artery bridging covered stent (BCS) occlusion.
sections.results: From 2011-2022, FEVAR was performed in 212 patients and BEVAR in 57. There were no statistical differences in demographics. The BEVAR group presented more frequently as urgencies (61% vs 11% for FEVAR p <,001). 955 TV were incorporated, including 536 RA. Technical success was 99%. BEVAR patients experienced higher perioperative death rates (14% vs 3% in FEVAR; p 0,005) and major complications (53% vs 17% in FEVAR; p <,001). Primary patency of RA in FEVAR was 99% at 3 years vs 74% for BEVAR (p < ,001). Freedom from RA BCS endoleaks were 97% at 3 years for the FEVAR group vs 87% in the BEVAR group (p <,001). Freedom from RA instability at 3 years was 95% in the FEVAR group vs 63% for the BEVAR group (p <,001). For CT-SMA only freedom from instability showed significant better outcomes at 3 years in the FEVAR group (96% vs 88% for BEVAR ; p ,006). In the multivariate analysis, the use of branches was the only factor associated with loss of patency in the RA.
sections.conclusion: In complex aortic repair for JAA, fenestrated devices achieved high patency rates while branched devices, mostly done for urgencies, are associated with significantly worse RA outcomes.

items.title: Risk factors associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.

sections.objective: To identify patient characteristics associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.
sections.methods: Retrospective cohort study. Children ≤18 years of age seen at a tertiary care children's hospital between 2009 and 2025 who were prescribed any type of steroid and had a documented intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation. Children with any IOP measurement >21 mmHg recorded prior to or on the day of steroid initiation were excluded. Steroid type, route of administration, and patient characteristics, including comorbidities, were extracted from the electronic medical record. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use.
sections.results: Of 5,687 children included (mean age at steroid initiation 8.8 years; 54.4% male), 1,034 (18.2%) developed ocular hypertension. The most frequently prescribed steroid was fluticasone (20.0%), and the most common route of administration was inhaled/intranasal (24.8%). In multivariable analysis, glaucoma conferred the highest odds of ocular hypertension after steroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.77; 95% CI, 5.21-8.79), followed by prednisone relative to dexamethasone (aOR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.30-4.93), juvenile arthritis (aOR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.09-2.24), and uveitis (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.16-1.99). Compared with topical administration, ocular (aOR, 3.57; 95% CI, 2.39-5.33) and intravenous (aOR, 2.63; 95% CI, 1.78-3.89) routes each independently conferred higher odds of ocular hypertension. Age, sex, race, ethnicity, diabetes, and asthma were not independently associated with ocular hypertension.
sections.conclusion: Nearly 1 in 5 children with an IOP measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation developed ocular hypertension. Glaucoma, uveitis, juvenile arthritis, and non-topical routes of administration-particularly ocular and intravenous-were the strongest risk factors, highlighting the importance of ophthalmic monitoring in children receiving glucocorticoid therapy.
sections.other: Ocular hypertension among children who underwent IOP measurement after steroid initiation, defined as IOP >21 mmHg measured within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of co-administered cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) 1·7 mg each and 1·0 mg each in adults with overweight or obesity (REDEFINE 9): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind within-dose-level, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3b trial.

sections.objective: Cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) 2·4 mg each has shown clinically meaningful bodyweight reductions in global phase 3 studies. Different dosing options might support individual treatment responses and tolerability. We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of once per week subcutaneous cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each or 1·0 mg each versus placebo in participants with obesity or overweight and at least one obesity-related complication.
sections.methods: This multicentre, randomised, double-blind within-dose-level, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3b trial (REDEFINE 9) was conducted across 24 sites in Canada, France, Germany, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older; with a BMI of at least 30 kg/m2 or at least 27 kg/m2 and one or more obesity-related complication; and without diabetes. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1:2:1) centrally, using block randomisation (block size of six) and a web-based system, to receive cagrilintide 1·7 mg plus semaglutide 1·7 mg (hereafter cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, starting at 0·25 mg each and escalated over 12 weeks), placebo 1·7 mg plus 1·7 mg (hereafter placebo 1·7 mg each), cagrilintide 1·0 mg plus semaglutide 1·0 mg (hereafter cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, starting at 0·25 mg each and escalated over 8 weeks), or placebo 1·0 mg plus 1·0 mg (hereafter placebo 1·0 mg each) for 68 weeks, plus nutrition and physical activity counselling until week 74. All treatments were administered subcutaneously once per week. The coprimary endpoints were relative mean change in bodyweight from baseline to week 68 and proportion of participants reaching a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% at week 68, assessed in the full analysis set (defined as all randomly assigned participants). Safety was assessed in the safety analysis set (defined as all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of the study drug). This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06388187 (completed).
sections.results: From June 24 to Oct 30, 2024, 333 participants were assessed for eligibility and 24 were excluded. 309 participants were randomly assigned (full analysis set: 104 assigned to cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, 103 to cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and 102 to pooled placebo). 308 participants received at least one dose of the study drug. 291 (94%) of 309 participants completed the study and 254 (82%) were on treatment at week 68. The mean age was 48·0 years (SD 13·6) and mean BMI was 39·1 kg/m2 (6·8). 239 (77%) participants were female, and 70 (23%) were male. For the efficacy estimand, the mean relative change from baseline in bodyweight at week 68 was -20·7% (SE 0·9) with cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, -21·0% (1·0) with cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and -2·0% (1·0) with the pooled placebo. Bodyweight reductions were significantly greater with both doses of cagrilintide-semaglutide than with placebo (estimated treatment difference [ETD] -18·8 percentage points [95% CI -21·5 to -16·0]; p<0·0001 for the 1·7 mg each dose and -19·0 percentage points [-21·8 to -16·2]; p<0·0001 for the 1·0 mg each dose). The proportion of participants reaching bodyweight reductions of at least 5% at week 68 was significantly greater with cagrilintide-semaglutide than with placebo (95·1% [SE 2·7] with the 1·7 mg each dose vs 33·4% [5·6] with placebo, ETD 61·7 percentage points [95% CI 49·5-74·0], p<0·0001; and 96·3% [2·2] with the 1·0 mg each dose, ETD 63·0 percentage points [51·1-74·9], p<0·0001). Adverse events were reported in 102 (99%) of 103 participants receiving cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, 98 (95%) of 103 receiving cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and 93 (91%) of 102 receiving the placebo. Most adverse events were mild or moderate and gastrointestinal-related. No deaths were reported.
sections.conclusion: Cagrilintide-semaglutide at 1·7 mg each and 1·0 mg each was superior to placebo at reducing bodyweight in adults with overweight or obesity, suggesting that different dose levels might support treatment flexibility.

items.title: Effects of plastic exposure on human health.
items.abstract: Plastic pollution is a critical environmental and public health challenge, with growing evidence linking human exposure to microplastics, nanoplastics, and associated chemicals to adverse health outcomes. This review summarises current knowledge on the health effects of plastic exposure, addressing both established findings and critical knowledge gaps. We examine human exposure to plastics and associated health risks based on available clinical and epidemiological evidence. Additionally, we explore chemicals associated with plastic, including their potential as carcinogens and disruptors of endocrine and immune function. Recognising the urgent need for preventive measures, we examine emerging strategies for reducing plastic burdens, including global regulatory efforts like the United Nations Plastics Treaty and proposed public health guidelines. By integrating current evidence, this review aims to provide a foundation for advancing research and informing strategies to mitigate health risks associated with plastic.

items.title: How I Do It: An Intensivist's guide to RV Failure and Right Ventricular Assist Devices.
items.abstract: Right ventricular failure (RVF) is a high-mortality form of cardiogenic shock frequently encountered in critical illness and is often underrecognized due to its heterogeneous presentation. This article presents a physiology-driven, stepwise approach to the diagnosis and management of acute RVF using a longitudinal case in the intensive care unit. We highlight practical bedside tools for recognition, including point-of-care ultrasound and invasive hemodynamics, and review targeted strategies for preload optimization, afterload reduction, and contractility support. Special emphasis is placed on airway management, vasoactive medications, and timely escalation to mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in appropriately selected patients. This bedside "How I Do It" guide is written for intensivists and pulmonary/critical care clinicians and translates advanced hemodynamic and device concepts into practical decision points for acute care management.

items.title: Comparative Effectiveness of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists versus DPP-4 and SGLT2 Inhibitors in Patients with Bronchiectasis and Type 2 Diabetes.

sections.objective: Bronchiectasis is a chronic inflammatory airway disease with limited disease-modifying therapies. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects, but their impact on bronchiectasis outcomes remains unknown.
sections.methods: Using the TriNetX global federated research network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes who initiated GLP-1RA therapy between June 1, 2022, and May 30, 2025. We compared clinical outcomes, including all-cause mortality, bronchiectasis exacerbation, acute respiratory failure, and lower respiratory tract infections, with patients receiving DPP-4i) or SGLT2i using propensity score matching to balance baseline characteristics.
sections.results: After propensity score matching, 1,029 patients per group were included in the GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i cohort, and 2,255 patients per group in the GLP-1RA versus SGLT2i cohort. Compared with DPP-4i, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.33-0.56) and reduced risks of acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.58) and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.46-0.65). Similar benefits were observed compared with SGLT2i for all-cause mortality (HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.40-0.60), acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.39-0.55), and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.68-0.86). Stratified analyses demonstrated consistent mortality benefits across demographic and clinical subgroups, with particularly pronounced effects in obese patients but there was no statistically significant reduction in bronchiectasis exacerbations.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significantly lower mortality and reduced respiratory complications compared with DPP-4i or SGLT2i. These findings suggest potential disease-modifying benefits of GLP-1RAs in bronchiectasis beyond glycemic control.
sections.other: Is GLP-1RA use, compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP-4i) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use, associated with better clinical outcomes in patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes (T2D)?

items.title: The Burden of Chronic Cough in Patients With Interstitial Lung Disease: a US Survey-Based Analysis of Its Effects on Daily Life and Emotional and Social Well-Being.

sections.objective: Chronic cough (≥8 weeks) is highly prevalent among patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and non-IPF interstitial lung disease (ILD) and imposes significant physical, social, and psychological burden. Research characterizing the burden of chronic cough in patients with IPF and non-IPF ILD from the patient perspective is limited.
sections.methods: An online cross-sectional survey was distributed to adults from June to July 2025 via the Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation's US Community Registry. Eligibility required a self-reported diagnosis of IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough. Multiple-choice and open-text questions spanned six domains: demographics, disease history, cough characteristics, daily life impact, social/emotional and long-term impact, and healthcare experience.
sections.results: A total of 197 participants completed the survey: 75.63% reported a diagnosis of IPF, 21.32% reported non-IPF ILD, and 3.05% were awaiting further ILD diagnosis. Participants reported cough-related interference with daily activities (76.15%) and sleep disruption (79.69%) within the preceding week. Emotional burden was frequently reported: 95.94% of participants had cough-induced worry, 75.13% had depression, sadness, or low mood, and 67.01% reported avoiding social situations because of cough. Additionally, 60.91% of participants reported that chronic cough affected their platonic relationships, and 55.33% reported impact on their ability or desire to maintain physical or intimate relationships. To treat cough, participants reported using an average of 2.7 therapeutic classes historically and 2.0 classes currently, with many reporting limited or no relief.
sections.conclusion: Findings from this US survey of patients with IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough indicate that, among respondents, chronic cough burden manifests physically, psychologically, and psychosocially. Reports of limited relief from available therapies suggest an unmet need in managing chronic cough in this patient population.
sections.other: What is the multidimensional burden of chronic cough in patients living with IPF or non-IPF ILD?

items.title: Single vs. Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after Fenestrated and Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

sections.objective: This study aimed to compare single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after fenestrated or branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR).
sections.results: Six retrospective cohorts comprising 3 623 patients were included, with 3 197 patients in separately extractable single or dual antiplatelet therapy groups. Several studies reported associations favouring dual antiplatelet therapy for target vessel patency. However, differences in outcome definitions, analytical units, and treatment classification precluded a common pooled estimate, and one association was attenuated after accounting for treatment changes. Evidence regarding ischaemic events, mortality, re-intervention, and endoleak was insufficient for reliable pooled comparisons. Five cohorts reported peri-operative bleeding using heterogeneous definitions and observation periods, of which a four study summary yielded an odds ratio of 1.30 (95% confidence interval 0.87 - 1.94) for dual vs. single antiplatelet therapy. Given the differences in outcome definitions, this does not estimate a common clinical effect.
sections.conclusion: The current evidence comparing single and dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR is based on heterogeneous cohort studies, focuses largely on surrogate outcomes such as target vessel patency, and shows no clear benefit for dual antiplatelet therapy. Comparative bleeding risk as well as clinical outcomes of single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR remain uncertain. Future prospective studies are needed to better delineate superiority of one regimen over the other.
sections.other: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global were searched from inception to 12 July 2026, with a supplementary targeted PubMed search on 5 September 2026. Comparative studies of post-operative antiplatelet therapy were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach. Outcomes were synthesised narratively when clinical and methodological differences precluded meaningful pooling; an additional quantitative summary of study defined bleeding outcomes was also reported.

items.title: Translocation of the environmental bacterium Aquitalea magnusonii promotes systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis in chronic liver disease.

sections.objective: Impaired mucosal barrier integrity facilitates translocation of the gut microbiome into the circulation and the liver, thereby exacerbating the severity of chronic liver diseases (CLD). This study aimed to investigate the pathogenic role of non-commensal environmental bacteria, specifically Aquitalea magnusonii in CLD progression by assessing its ability to cross the intestinal barrier and induce systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis.
sections.methods: Using an integrated translational framework, patient blood analyses were combined with multi-omics profiling, human intestinal epithelial models, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), hepatic stellate cells (HSC), monocytes, and alcoholic (ALD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated (MASLD) models to evaluate the translocation, virulence, inflammatory and fibrotic potential of A. magnusonii in CLD.
sections.results: Non-commensal environmental bacteria, including Aquitalea spp. were detected in multiple organs in both ALD and MASLD models. Detection of Aquitalea DNA in patient samples and other non-commensal environmental bacteria in tap water suggested potential aquatic reservoirs. A. magnusonii produced 12 acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) associated metabolites and its outer membrane vesicles (OMV) were enriched in virulence-related proteins, supporting roles in adhesion, invasion, and immune activation. In addition, gavage with A. magnusonii led to a substantial dysbiotic shift in the gut microbiome. Mechanistically, the cell-free supernatant of A. magnusonii culture activated TLR2- and TLR4-dependent pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. Exposure to A. magnusonii or its pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) significantly increased inflammation and fibrosis in vitro and in vivo.
sections.conclusion: Non-commensal environmental bacteria, in the example of A. magnusonii, can translocate across the intestinal barrier and promote liver inflammation and fibrogenesis via metabolite production, virulence-associated OMV, and innate immune activation.
sections.other: This study highlights an underrecognized role of non-commensal environmental bacteria in chronic liver disease. Beyond gut commensals, detection of non-commensal environmental microbes such as Aquitalea was associated with markers of more advanced liver disease, while experimental studies of A. magnusonii support biological plausibility for a potential contributory role. These findings highlight the importance of considering environmental reservoirs and non-commensal pathogens in microbial contributions to CLD pathogenesis.

items.title: Circulating tumor DNA to direct adjuvant immunotherapy across mismatch repair-deficient solid tumors.

sections.objective: Detection of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) harboring mutations that match those identified in resected tumor tissue signals occult residual disease after curative-intent surgery. Such patients are considered minimal residual disease (MRD)-positive and at high risk for recurrence and death. Few studies have shown that therapeutic intervention can alter recurrence risk in MRD-positive patients. We evaluated whether PD-1 blockade could reduce recurrence in MRD-positive patients with mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) tumors after curative-intent resection regardless of tumor site of origin.
sections.methods: We initiated a prospective phase II interventional study in patients who had undergone curative-intent resection of early-stage dMMR tumors from any anatomic site. Postoperative MRD status was assessed by first identifying those patients who had detectable ctDNA and then confirming the ctDNA relevance to MRD by matching mutations detected in ctDNA to somatic mutations detected in resected tumor tissue. Confirmed MRD-positive patients received 6 months of PD-1 blockade and were evaluated for ctDNA clearance and 24-month recurrence-free survival (RFS). MRD-negative patients underwent observation.
sections.results: We screened 184 patients with early-stage dMMR solid tumors after curative resection and tumor sequencing with ctDNA testing for MRD assessment. Twenty-three patients (12.5%) were MRD-positive; after excluding one assigned to placebo and three with synchronous radiographic disease, 19 were eligible. Six developed recurrences before pembrolizumab initiation despite being disease-free at enrollment. The remaining 13 MRD-positive patients received 6 months of PD-1 blockade. ctDNA clearance at 6 months was achieved in 11 of 13 patients (85%). Five treated patients (38%) developed recurrence during follow-up. Median follow-up for the MRD-positive patients was 59 months (95% CI: 52-NR). Among 152 MRD-negative patients managed with observation, 14 (9%) developed recurrence during follow-up; 2-year RFS was 92%.
sections.conclusion: These findings provide evidence that ctDNA-guided adjuvant therapy may offer clinical benefit in dMMR tumors regardless of tissue of origin.

items.title: The functional significance of human macular pigment: Optical, visual and neural effects.
items.abstract: The foveal region of primates is specialized to accumulate dietary yellow carotenoids, lutein (L) and zeaxanthin (Z) which collectively form the macular pigment (MP). These pigments selectively attenuate short-wave visible light. Although MP is often regarded mostly for its protective role in reducing photo-oxidative damage to the retina, its functional significance to everyday vision is becoming increasingly apparent. Psychophysical methods have been used for decades to measure the pigments showing direct connections to visual function. Evidence is accumulating, however, that the optical effects of MP alter perception under natural viewing conditions. For instance, increasing MP density through intervention enhances chromatic contrast, improves target visibility through simulated atmospheric blue haze, reduces glare disability and discomfort, and speeds recovery from photostress. Conversely, evidence that these optical filtering properties improve conventional visual acuity or contrast sensitivity by reducing chromatic aberration remains limited. Beyond these optical mechanisms, L and Z may also exert biochemical and cellular effects. L and Z accumulate in central nervous system tissue, where intervention studies suggest potential effects on visual processing speed, attention, memory, and neural efficiency. Emerging evidence also supports localized and systemic roles for these carotenoids in retinal development and structure and metabolic regulation. MP density varies by more than an order of magnitude among healthy individuals; while this implies corresponding individual variation in optical filtering, further research is required to determine if this variation extends proportionally to the wider structural, functional, and metabolic effects of these carotenoids.

items.title: Making patient-reported outcomes reusable at scale.
items.abstract: Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) are essential to understanding how people live with illness, treatment, and care, and are increasingly promoted for routine use in clinical practice, quality improvement, and value-based health care. PROs are also increasingly relevant in digital health and artificial intelligence applications, both as inputs to predictive models and as outputs reflecting patient-centred aspects of health. Yet, PROs remain difficult to reuse at scale: their implementation is inconsistent across health-care settings, measurement approaches are highly heterogeneous, and PROs are rarely available as large, standardised, analysable datasets suitable for multisite analyses and advanced analytics, including artificial intelligence models. In this Viewpoint, we argue that the central challenge is not a lack of initiatives, but the absence of a coherent, end-to-end approach that connects measurement, routine capture, data standards, and analytic reuse. We propose a practical four-step pathway towards Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) PROs. This pathway focuses on (1) defining the outcome domains that matter and selecting high-quality questionnaires; (2) capturing PROs consistently at the point of care in structured, computable formats; (3) storing them in analysable, shareable data models; and (4) establishing transparent cross-questionnaire linking to enable comparable scores. None of these steps poses major technical challenges in isolation; the primary difficulty is that these efforts are often developed in silos, with minimal coordination across disciplines, from questionnaire development and validation to clinical workflows, informatics standards, analytic infrastructures, and governance. A shared FAIR-PROs approach would allow PROs to become a routine, reusable component of learning health systems and a driver of both person-centred care and data-driven innovation.

items.title: Harmonising difficult-to-manage and complex-to-manage psoriatic arthritis: from divergent prevalence estimates to reproducible, mechanism-aware phenotypes.
items.abstract: Difficult-to-manage or complex-to-manage psoriatic arthritis is increasingly recognised in clinical practice, but prevalence estimates remain difficult to interpret because studies differ in denominators, definitions of treatment failure, and methods for distinguishing persistent symptoms from objective inflammation. Building on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology difficult-to-manage definition and the Group for Research and Assessment of Psoriasis and Psoriatic Arthritis complex-to-manage definition, this Viewpoint proposes an implementation framework to improve reproducibility across registries, trials, and translational studies. We recommend dual-denominator reporting, with estimates presented both in all patients with psoriatic arthritis and in patients exposed to biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. We also propose an auditable treatment ledger documenting drug mechanism and class, adequacy of exposure, optimisation attempts, and reasons for discontinuation. After treatment-pathway difficulty is established, patients should be stratified by dominant drivers of persistent burden: inflammatory, non-inflammatory, or mixed. Domain-specific description, impact profiling, disease duration, and prespecified sensitivity analyses should improve comparability and interpretation.

items.title: Land use, common agricultural policy subsidies, and farm economic exposure under planetary health diet scenarios in Europe: a physical input-output modelling analysis.

sections.objective: Animal-sourced food (ASF) production dominates agricultural land use in the EU and attracts a large share of public fiscal support. Although shifts away from ASFs have broad implications for land use, public spending, and farming livelihoods, the distributional effects across regions and supply chains remain largely unquantified. This study aims to quantify these effects and identify regional differences in the economic implications of transitioning towards plant-rich diets.
sections.methods: We assessed the effects of adopting the planetary health diet (PHD) and its variants across the EU+UK relative to a 2020 baseline. Using the multiregional food and agriculture biomass input-output model, we linked farm income and labour accounts to agricultural supply, use, and trade to trace feed-animal-food linkages through supply chains. We summarised regional heterogeneity using six transition archetypes defined by sectoral composition, profitability excluding subsidies, and reliance on livestock.
sections.results: Adopting the PHD would release 58-78 million hectares of agricultural land in the EU+UK and free up €28-36 billion per year of common agricultural policy (CAP) subsidies under increasingly plant-rich variants of the PHD. Correspondingly, EU+UK farm employment would decline by 37-40% and farm profits excluding CAP subsidies would decrease by 15% (PHD) to 3% (PHD-vegan). These effects varied across regions: in places where livestock production was loss-making at baseline (excluding CAP subsidies), reduced ASF demand could eliminate these losses and increase regional profits; in contrast, profits declined in regions where livestock production was profitable.
sections.conclusion: Dietary change creates substantial scope for land and fiscal repurposing; however, transition costs are concentrated geographically and across production systems. The diversity in regional archetypes will require differentiated support to achieve a plant-rich and just food transition, which could be partly financed via repurposed CAP resources.

items.title: Community health worker-led hypertension management with independent prescribing in rural Lesotho: a cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial.

sections.objective: Hypertension is the leading global risk factor for premature mortality, yet treatment coverage and control remain poor, particularly in low-income and middle-income countries. Whether community health workers can manage hypertension, including independent prescribing and titrating of antihypertensive therapy, remains unknown. We aimed to assess whether hypertension care led by community health workers with independent prescribing was non-inferior to usual facility-based care for maintaining blood pressure control among adults with treated, controlled hypertension.
sections.methods: We conducted a pragmatic, cluster-randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial in 103 villages in rural Lesotho. Adults with treated, controlled hypertension (<140/90 mm Hg) were eligible. Villages were randomly assigned 1:1, stratified by district and access to health facility, by an independent statistician using a computer-generated sequence to hypertension care led by community health workers, including independent prescribing and titrating of antihypertensive therapy (amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide combination pills at doses of 5 mg amlodipine and 12·5 mg hydrochlorothiazide or 10 mg amlodipine and 25 mg hydrochlorothiazide) with clinical decision support, or to usual nurse-led, facility-based care. The primary endpoint was blood pressure control at 12 months among all randomised participants except individuals who became pregnant during follow-up, with a non-inferiority margin of -10 percentage points absolute risk difference. The study has been completed and is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05684055).
sections.results: Between Sept 8, 2023, and May 31, 2024, we enrolled 807 participants (417 in 51 control villages, 390 in 50 intervention villages; two empty clusters; mean age 64·4 years [SD 14·3]; 82% female). At 12 months, blood pressure was controlled in 300 (78%) of 386 participants in the intervention group and 303 (74%) of 412 in the control group (adjusted odds ratio 1·29, 95% CI 0·93-1·80); non-inferiority was met. The adjusted absolute risk difference was 5·1% (95% CI -0·9 to 11·2). Serious adverse events (deaths and hospitalisations) were similar in the two groups, with no excess events attributed to the intervention.
sections.conclusion: These findings support community-based hypertension care with task-sharing to trained community health workers as a promising approach to maintaining blood pressure control, especially in settings with limited access to physician-led and nurse-led hypertension care.

items.title: Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.
items.abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a subset of these candidates. All 28 emerged directly from the mechanistic model structure and multi-omics constraints, with no calibration to known drug targets or cancer-dependency data. Simulations of thymidylate synthase, hexokinase, and triokinase inhibition predicted target- and physiology-specific changes in pathway use, energy metabolism, and a shared ceramide-linked stress response. Mapping predicted enzyme-activity shifts to BRCA1-associated transcription factors suggested regulatory routes underlying differences between the two states. These ensembles provide a reusable framework for time-resolved, mechanistic hypothesis generation across cancers and other diseases. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

items.title: All-optical sensing of dermal activity enables an AI-powered wearable ring for continuous stress monitoring.
items.abstract: Electrodermal activity (EDA), a primary stress-sensing signal in today's wearables, requires skin-electrode contact that drifts and degrades over time, limiting long-term use. Here, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered ring for all-optical sensing of dermal activity (ODA), using light rather than electrodes to track sweat gland activation, thereby enhancing durability and comfort. An optimized dual-wavelength design (960 and 1250 nanometers) captures perspiration dynamics while concurrently recording photoplethysmography. The ODA ring integrates temperature and motion sensors for multimodal monitoring with on-device inference. In correlation studies, ODA and EDA signals showed 86% agreement. In classification tasks, the ODA ring achieved 92.3% binary accuracy versus 77.95% for EDA. In multiclass tasks, ODA outperforms EDA by 100 to 74.58% (short term) and 89.72 to 43.20% (long term). On-device one-dimensional convolutional neural network inference enabled 87.53% autonomous accuracy. This electrode-free modality establishes a scalable, all-optical platform for rings, watches, and patches for accurate, robust, and long-term stress monitoring.

items.title: Safety and Efficacy of Transvenous Lead Extraction Using a Right-Sided Approach.

sections.objective: Despite extensive experience with transvenous lead extraction (TLE) overall, outcomes for systems implanted on the right chest remain underexplored, largely because of their low incidence. The objective was to evaluate whether system laterality influences TLE outcomes.
sections.methods: Using our institutional, prospectively maintained ExTRACT registry, we analyzed all consecutive patients undergoing TLE procedures at the Cleveland Clinic between 1996 and 2022. Patients were categorized by system laterality. Baseline characteristics, procedural characteristics, and complications were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the association between right-sided TLE and adverse events.
sections.results: Among 4,989 patients, 494 (9.9%) had right-sided and 4,495 (90.1%) had left-sided TLE. Compared with left-sided cases, right-sided cases had longer total lead dwell times (13.83 vs 9.26 years, P < 0.001) and were more likely to be extracted because of infection (47.57% vs 39.71%, P = 0.001). Fluoroscopy time was longer (15.95 vs 12.1 minutes; P < 0.001), and femoral workstation use more frequent (7.89% vs 4.05%, P < 0.001), yet complete extraction was lower (94.53% vs 96.44%, P = 0.034). Right-sided TLE had higher rates of sternotomy (2.83% vs 1.25%, P = 0.004) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (2.49% vs 1.10%, P = 0.009). Thirty-day mortality was low and comparable (0.61% vs 0.47%, P = 0.727). Multivariable regression showed that right-sided TLE was associated with higher odds of sternotomy (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.01-3.46, P = 0.037) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (OR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.01-3.78, P = 0.037).
sections.conclusion: Right-sided TLE is associated with a lower rate of complete extraction and increased procedural risk, particularly sternotomy and major vascular injury, compared with left-sided TLE. These findings should be carefully weighed when implanting or extracting right-sided systems.

items.title: Brain health in children born extremely preterm: a multidimensional perspective.
items.abstract: Gestational age and developmental stage of the brain at birth are major determinants of child health, and long-term consequences of preterm birth and altered brain maturation are inadequately understood simply through brain injury, survival rates, or diagnostic labels. In this Review, we conceptualise brain health in children born extremely preterm (before 28 weeks' gestation) as a developmental condition shaped by maturational timing, biological vulnerability, neonatal intensive care exposure, sensory and relational experiences, family circumstances, and social environments. We integrate evidence from research on early brain development and consciousness, long-term multidomain neurodevelopmental outcomes, neonatal intensive care practice, relational caregiving, early developmental interventions, and ethical, psychological, and social dimensions of care. Across these domains, extremely preterm birth emerges not as a single event but as a neuroplastic system that adapts to biological and environmental risks and protective factors that shape neurodevelopmental resilience and vulnerabilities and establish developmental trajectories. We argue that care for the infant born extremely preterm is optimised through a brain-health framework where care becomes a longitudinal, ethical process that integrates family support, minimises harmful exposures, promotes adaptive development, and fosters participation, wellbeing, and quality of life.

items.title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes.
sections.methods: Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial. 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study. Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years.
sections.results: 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01).
sections.conclusion: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume.
sections.other: 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China. The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume.

items.title: Lynch syndrome.
items.abstract: Lynch syndrome is the most common inherited cancer predisposition syndrome, affecting approximately one in 350-450 individuals, yet the majority of carriers remain undiagnosed, representing a substantial and preventable public health burden. Caused by germline pathogenic variants in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes, Lynch syndrome confers markedly elevated and heterogeneous risks of colorectal, endometrial, and multiple extracolonic cancers. Advances in molecular diagnostics, particularly universal tumour testing for MMR deficiency, have transformed case identification and enabled targeted germline testing and cascade screening of relatives at risk. Despite these advances, implementation remains inconsistent, with substantial attrition across diagnostic pathways and inequities in access to care. Preventive strategies-including colonoscopic surveillance, aspirin chemoprevention, and risk-reducing surgery-are effective but require gene-specific and individualised application. Therapeutically, the immunogenic biology of MMR-deficient tumours has positioned Lynch syndrome at the forefront of precision oncology, with immune checkpoint inhibitors delivering substantial benefit and emerging vaccine strategies offering promise for cancer interception. In this Review, we provide an integrated overview of Lynch syndrome across the continuum of care, highlighting advances in biology, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment, while emphasising the crucial need to align scientific progress with equitable and effective health-system delivery.

items.title: Harmonized brain ontology and 3D atlases for human, macaque, and marmoset basal ganglia.
items.abstract: A major goal of the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is to create a suite of foundational reference cell atlases and associated standards for human and nonhuman primate brains. Central to this goal is the creation of cross-species-harmonized cellular taxonomies and structural parcellations with formal ontologies that can be mapped onto 3D reference frameworks, bridging neuroimaging and cellular and histological resolutions. We describe an iterative approach, focused initially on the basal ganglia, to co-create structural and cellular ontologies for human, macaque, and marmoset brains and to map and refine structural parcellations into neuroimaging-based common coordinate frameworks. We create a Harmonized Ontology of Mammalian Brain Anatomy (HOMBA) to meet these needs. These references provide the framework for documenting and mapping all experimental sampling in BICAN, allowing analyses of cellular and molecular variation as a function of topographic position and enabling comparisons of cellular, molecular, and neuroimaging-based functional variation across species.

items.title: An integrative single-cell epigenomic atlas annotates the regulatory genome of the adult mouse brain.
items.abstract: Histone modifications underpin the cell-type-specific gene regulatory programs that drive the remarkable cellular diversity of the mammalian brain. Here, we jointly profiled four histone modifications and the transcriptome in 2.5 million nuclei from the adult mouse brain. By integrating these data with chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and three-dimensional genome organization, we constructed a unified epigenomic atlas spanning over 100 brain cell subclasses and assigned active, primed, and repressive chromatin states across 81% of the genome. Active chromatin states marked by combinatorial histone modifications better nominate candidate enhancers with functional support than chromatin accessibility alone, while H3K27me3- and H3K9me3-marked chromatin states delineate distinct modes of cell-type-specific gene repression. Finally, this multimodal resource enables the development of deep learning models that predict cell-type-specific epigenomic features and gene expression from DNA sequence, providing a comprehensive framework for annotating the brain regulatory genome and interpreting non-coding disease risk variants.

items.title: Single-cell, multi-region profiling of the macaque brain across the lifespan.
items.abstract: Brain aging is a complex process with profound health and societal consequences. However, the molecular and cellular pathways that govern its progression, and inter- and intra-individual variation, remain poorly defined. We present a transcriptomic atlas of 5.3 million cells from 582 samples spanning 11 brain regions of 55 rhesus macaques (aged 0.5-21 years). We identify age-depleted and vulnerable neuronal populations and subtle, age-associated compositional differences in glia-detectable only at single-cell resolution. We chart convergent and divergent age-associated molecular signatures across regions and cell types, which include sex-specific signatures that could underlie biases in neurological disorders. These signatures overlap those of Alzheimer's disease (AD), which suggests that aging and AD share molecular roots that emerge at different ages and in region- and sex-specific windows of vulnerability. This work provides a temporal, regional, and sex-stratified atlas of the aging primate brain, offering insights into cell-type-specific vulnerabilities and regional heterogeneity with translational human relevance.

items.title: A single-cell and spatial 3D multi-omic atlas of developing human basal ganglia.
items.abstract: Human basal ganglia (BG) neurons and inhibitory interneurons originate in the ganglionic eminences (GEs), transient structures in the ventral prenatal brain. This study delineates the specification and maturation of GEs and GE-derived neurons using single-nucleus methyl-3C sequencing (snm3C-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and single-molecule chromatin + RNA imaging, and we found heterogeneous temporal progression across GE subregions. Spiny projection neurons (SPNs), the principal cells of the BG, acquire distinct subtypes through synchronized 3D-epigenomic remodeling, in contrast to the asynchronous maturation of other neuron types. Oligodendrocyte differentiation involves a transient short-range chromatin state during infancy, showing that the short-range and long-range chromatin conformations previously linked to terminal glial and neuronal fates can also be transient. The temporal cortex matured epigenomically faster than other cortical regions during this period. Lastly, SPNs were enriched in genetic risk for neuropsychiatric disease. Our study extends findings on unique 3D-epigenomic dynamics during human brain development.

items.title: Disruption of cell-type-specific molecular programs of striatal spiny projection neurons in autism.
items.abstract: Rare genetic variants contribute substantially to autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet the regulatory logic of vulnerable subcortical cells is poorly understood. In a 16p11.2 deletion mouse model, lineage tracing across five brain regions revealed prominent striatal changes. In the human putamen from ASD and neurotypical donors, single-nucleus multi-omics showed transcriptional alterations concentrated in D1 striosome spiny projection neurons (SPNs), affecting synaptic and energy metabolism genes, with altered synapse-supporting programs in astrocytes. Gene regulatory network analysis integrating chromatin accessibility and expression identified EGR1 and EGR3 as key regulators of these programs, with reduced activity in D1 striosome SPNs. Deleting EGR1 or EGR3 in human striatal organoids produced partially overlapping transcriptional changes. These findings establish the striatum as a site of molecular convergence in ASD and provide a multi-omic resource for dissecting subcortical mechanisms.

items.title: Circuit-aligned specialization of human basal ganglia astrocytes.
items.abstract: Astrocytes shape synapses and circuits, yet their diversity within the human basal ganglia remains poorly defined. Integrating single-nucleus transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with spatial transcriptomics, we identify three anatomically organized astrocyte subgroups-striatal gray matter (GM), extra-striatal GM, and white matter (WM)-distinguished by neurotransmitter transporter expression and synapse-associated programs that reflect afferent input. These molecular distinctions generalize brain-wide, separating telencephalic from non-telencephalic astrocytes, with LHX2 marking telencephalic astrocyte identity across species. Within the striatum (STR), dorsal and ventral populations align with distinct microcircuits; a ventral population maps to the nucleus accumbens mediodorsal shell alongside specialized neuronal subtypes, a pattern conserved in nonhuman primates. A deep learning sequence model identifies subgroup-specific enhancer codes and recovers established transcription factor motif logic from published enhancer-AAV datasets, providing a foundation for targeted viral vector design. These findings define intersecting axes of human astrocyte specialization and offer a framework for cell-type-specific dissection of basal ganglia circuits.

items.title: Morphoelectric diversity and specialization of primate striatal neuron types.
items.abstract: The basal ganglia are evolutionarily ancient subcortical nuclei that form interconnected loops with the neocortex and limbic system to regulate movement, learning, habit formation, emotion, and motivation. Their dysfunction contributes to major neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet most cellular-level insights derive from rodent studies, leaving knowledge gaps in humans and translationally relevant primate species. To address this, we generated multimodal Patch-seq data linking transcriptomic identity with morphological and electrophysiological properties in the macaque striatum-the input nucleus of the basal ganglia. We found underappreciated diversity among spiny projection neurons (SPNs), including non-canonical types, and variation aligned with functional gradients. Interneurons also exhibited spatial variation and even greater morphoelectric diversity, highlighting their functional modularity. Despite broad evolutionary conservation, we identified primate-specific features and key differences from rodent striatal neurons. By integrating molecular classification with cellular properties that shape network function, our findings provide insights into the functional organization of the primate striatum.

items.title: Spatial and regulatory organization of cell identity across the primate subcortex.
items.abstract: Mammalian brain cell identity is shaped by intrinsic factors and external context. We present a spatially resolved transcriptomic and gene regulatory atlas of cell types across all subcortical regions in a primate, the common marmoset. Dense sampling and cross-species integration revealed spatially precise neuronal assemblies, including ones in complex midbrain and diencephalic structures. Chromatin accessibility and transcriptional identity are spatially tuned within and across subcortical structures; spatial gradients within hippocampal subfields are orchestrated by graded transcription factors acting through graded enhancers. The primate-expanded thalamic γ-aminobutyric acid (GABAergic) population shares transcriptional and regulatory syntax with conserved midbrain populations, reflecting an evolutionary adaptation compared with rodents. Similar regional expression across cell types can arise by distinct regulatory architectures, as observed in telencephalic astrocytes and neurons. Conversely, distant cell types can share regulatory programs despite divergent identities: striatal GABAergic spiny projection neurons and telencephalic glutamatergic neurons share a postsynaptic regulatory program despite divergent lineages, regions, and neurotransmitter identities.

items.title: Single-cell multimodal atlas reveals regulatory programs in the human brain.
items.abstract: Direct measurement of chromatin states together with transcription is essential for understanding how cell-type-specific regulatory programs are established and maintained in the adult human brain. Here, we present a large-scale single-cell multimodal atlas by jointly profiling the transcriptome with active (H3K27ac) or repressive (H3K27me3) histone modifications across 18 adult brain regions.
