Hospitals using a 0/3 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h) as standard care were randomly allocated to implement the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) after 6 months (early implementation) or 12 months (late implementation). The trial was designed to test the non-inferiority of the 0/1 h pathway for safety and its superiority for efficacy. The non-inferiority margin was set at an odds ratio of 1·3. Analyses were done in the full analysis set. The coprimary safety outcome was a composite of death from any cause or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, and the coprimary efficacy outcome was emergency department length of stay. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05649384, and is active but no longer enrolling.
sections.results: Between Dec 1, 2020, and Dec 31, 2024, 71 983 consecutive patient presentations were screened, of which 67 624 (93·9%) met the eligibility criteria and comprised the full analysis set. Median age was 59 years (IQR 46-73); 29 954 (44·3%) patient presentations were in female patients and 37 670 (55·7%) were in male patients. 13 753 (22·2%) of 62 060 patient presentations with available data were in patients with known coronary artery disease, and 5855 (8·7%) patient presentations had an adjudicated index diagnosis of myocardial infarction. Overall, 36 464 patient presentations were managed with a 0/3 h pathway and 31 160 with the 0/1 h pathway. Death from any cause or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 454 (1·2%) patient presentations in the 0/3 h group and in 341 (1·1%) patient presentations in the 0/1 h group (adjusted odds ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·77-1·13]; pnon-inferiority=0·0004). The median emergency department length of stay was 309 min (IQR 203-470) in the 0/3 h pathway and 309 min (207-474) in the 0/1 h pathway (ratio of adjusted median times 1·00 [95% CI 0·97-1·02]; two-sided p=0·65).
sections.conclusion: Implementation of the 0/1 h pathway met the prespecified non-inferiority criterion for the 30-day composite safety outcome but did not shorten emergency department length of stay compared with the 0/3 h pathway. In this setting, implementation of the 0/1 h pathway alone should therefore not be expected to improve emergency department throughput.

items.title: Generalised eruptive histiocytosis mimicking lymphoma relapse in a patient with previous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
items.abstract: A 92-year-old man with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated with chemoradiotherapy, and later with radiotherapy for an isolated cutaneous relapse with complete response, presented with a 1-month history of multiple asymptomatic erythematous-to-violaceous papules and nodules on the face, trunk, and upper limbs. Given his oncological history and previous skin involvement, lymphoma relapse was the leading diagnostic concern, with cutaneous metastases and sarcoidosis also considered. However, skin biopsies showed a non-Langerhans cell histiocytic infiltrate expressing CD45, CD68, and CD163, without CD1a, CD20, PAX5, S100, or Langerin expression. Skin and blood flow cytometry identified no abnormal cell populations, and a PET-CT scan showed no abnormal metabolic activity. Clinicopathological correlation narrowed the differential to group C (cutaneous) histiocytosis, and subsequent spontaneous regression of the lesions over 3 months without treatment supported the diagnosis of generalised eruptive histiocytosis. At 15 months of follow-up, there was no recurrence or evidence of active disease. This case illustrates that cutaneous histiocytoses can mimic several inflammatory and neoplastic conditions, including lymphoma relapse, reinforcing the need to actively resist cognitive bias in people who have had cancer through reflective reassessment, broad differential diagnosis, and biopsy confirmation.

items.title: Pegcetacoplan for geographic atrophy: Bridging the "clinical relevance gap" through precision medicine.
items.abstract: The approval of pegcetacoplan marks a transformative era in the management of geographic atrophy (GA), offering the first FDA-approved intervention to slow lesion growth. A critical analysis of accumulated data, however, reveals a profound "clinical relevance gap." While pegcetacoplan demonstrates a measurable reduction in GA progression, this anatomical benefit exhibits a striking dissociation from high-acuity visual acuity gains, though emerging data suggests preservation of microperimetric function. We narrative synthesize evidence from pivotal trials, real-world studies, and advanced imaging analyses to interrogate the mechanistic rationale of upstream C3 inhibition, the "CNV Paradox" where therapy exchanges dry atrophy progression for increased exudative conversion, and the risk redistribution inherent in chronic complement blockade. We evaluate the burden of high-frequency intravitreal injections, the implications of rare but devastating inflammatory events like retinal vasculitis, and the limitations of current imaging endpoints. We argue that the therapeutic potential of pegcetacoplan is maximized not by a "treat-all" approach, but through a precision medicine paradigm. Identifying patients with specific biomarkers such as a high ellipsoid zone to retinal pigment epithelium loss ratio bridges the gap between structural preservation and functional relevance, ensuring that the risks of therapy are outweighed by meaningful clinical benefit.

items.title: Statin Use and Age-related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Disease Outcomes.

sections.methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through October 2025 for randomized trials and cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies with comparators. We assessed risk of bias with tools appropriate to each design and pooled effect measures separately using random-effects models. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO.
sections.results: Twenty-eight studies included 1,918,120 participants. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) for the prevalence of any, early, and late AMD were 1.03 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-1.24), 1.10 (95% CI, 0.92-1.31), and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.46-1.25), respectively. For incidence of any AMD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) was 1.04 (95% CI, 0.82-1.31) and the OR was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.43-1.34), with substantial heterogeneity. For neovascular AMD incidence, different study subsets suggested lower hazard (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.60-0.85) and higher risk (risk ratio, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.44); the OR was inconclusive (0.93; 95% CI, 0.82-1.05). Progression evidence was limited and heterogeneous. Ten of 12 longitudinal nonrandomized studies had serious overall risk of bias.
sections.conclusion: The evidence was of very low certainty and insufficient to establish a protective or harmful effect of statins on AMD. These findings do not support prescribing statins specifically for AMD or discontinuing otherwise indicated therapy.
sections.other: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between statin use and the prevalence, incidence, and progression of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). AMD is a major cause of vision loss in older adults, many of whom receive statins for cardiovascular prevention.

items.title: Fixed Dose Inferior Oblique Recession Has Self-Adjusting Effect.

sections.objective: This study aimed to determine the effect of a uniform dose of unilateral inferior oblique muscle (IO) recession on incomitant hypertropia.
sections.methods: Retrospective consecutive case series. Patients underwent unilateral IO recession by a single surgeon who reinserted the IO 4 mm posterior and 3 mm temporal to the temporal pole of the inferior rectus insertion. Hypertropia was measured in distant central and secondary gazes, and centrally at near. Surgical effects were evaluated by linear regression.
sections.results: Mean patient age was 40±27 (standard deviation) years, and follow-up averaged 448±562 days. Twenty patients had superior oblique palsy. Mean hypertropia in central gaze decreased after IO recession from 8.8±7.9Δ to 1.2±2.9Δ, and in contralateral gaze from 17.0±9.6Δ to 2.1±3.6Δ. Mean preoperative horizontal incomitance decreased after IO recession from 13.7±8.4Δ to 2.4±4.1Δ. Mean vertical incomitance decreased from 6.8Δ to 2.0±4.4Δ. Surgical effect was proportionately greater with greater preoperative hypertropia, resulting on average in nearly ideal correction of all hypertropia at distance in central, ipsilateral, contralateral, as well as in near gazes. This effect generally eliminated incomitance. Three (9%) patients required additional strabismus treatment.
sections.conclusion: Fixed-dose IO recession corrects a wide range of incomitant hypertropia in a self-grading manner, achieving excellent effect for a wide range of hypertropia and incomitance.
sections.other: Thirty-three patients with incomitant hypertropia who underwent identical unilateral IO recession between June 2015 and June 2025. Postoperative hypertropia, incomitance, retreatment, and relationship of initial deviation to surgical effect.

items.title: Amrecibart and cenvacibart for the prevention of catheter-related thrombosis (ROXI-CATH): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: Peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are often complicated by venous thromboembolism, yet no thromboprophylaxis is approved. Factor XI (FXI) inhibition might prevent catheter-associated venous thromboembolism without increasing bleeding. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of amrecibart and cenvacibart for preventing venous thromboembolism after PICC placement.
sections.methods: ROXI-CATH is a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial conducted across 12 hospital centres in Bulgaria, Canada, Israel, Romania, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants aged 18 years or older undergoing PICC insertion, with the PICC expected to remain for at least 14 days, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 or less were randomly assigned (1:1:1) using a permuted block design and stratified by site and diagnosis of active cancer to receive a single intravenous infusion of amrecibart (300 mg; anti-FXI A2 domain monoclonal antibody), cenvacibart (250 mg; anti-FXI catalytic domain monoclonal antibody), or placebo. Participants, principal investigators, and study site staff were masked to treatment assignment. The primary efficacy outcome was adjudicated venous thromboembolism (symptomatic or asymptomatic PICC-associated deep vein thrombosis or superficial vein thrombosis, or pulmonary embolism, including pulmonary embolism-related death) up to day 14. Ultrasounds were performed on days 7 and 14. The key secondary efficacy outcome was adjudicated thrombosis detected by ultrasound in the upper extremity with the PICC up to day 14. The primary safety outcome was site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to the end of the study. The key secondary safety outcomes were adjudicated major and clinically relevant non-major (CRNM) bleeding up to day 14. Efficacy analyses were performed in the full analysis set, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug and with any evaluable post-baseline ultrasound or a confirmed episode of venous thromboembolism. Safety analyses were performed in the safety analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug (as treated). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299111 (completed; these analyses were performed after database lock on May 6, 2026).
sections.results: Between Sept 20, 2024, and Dec 19, 2025, 240 participants were screened, and 195 were randomly assigned to amrecibart (n=65), cenvacibart (n=66), or placebo (n=64). One participant in the placebo group who did not receive study treatment and had no evaluable ultrasound was excluded from the full analysis set. The median follow-up time was 100 days (IQR 100-103). The median age was 60 years (49-69), and 89 (46%) of 194 participants were female, 105 (54%) were male, and 192 (99%) were White. Adjudicated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occured in 13 (20%) of 65 participants in the amrecibart group (odds ratio [OR] 0·37 [90% credible interval 0·18-0·65]), 13 (20%) of 66 participants in the cenvacibart group (0·36 [0·17-0·64]) compared with 27 (43%) of 63 participants in the placebo group. Adjudicated PICC-associated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occurred in 12 (18%) participants in the amrecibart group (OR 0·30 [95% CI 0·14-0·67]), 13 (20%) participants in the cenvacibart group (0·32 [0·14-0·69]), compared with 27 (43%) participants in the placebo group. Site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to day 100 occurred in 45 (69%) participants in the amrecibart group, 42 (64%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and 48 (76%) participants in the placebo group. No participants had major bleeding up to day 14. CRNM bleeding up to day 14 occurred in two (3%) participants in the amrecibart group, two (3%) in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred in nine (14%) participants in the ambrecibart group, six (9%) in the cenvacibart group, and ten (16%) in the placebo group. One (2%) participant in the amrecibart group, four (6%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) participants in the placebo group died; these deaths were assessed as not related to treatment by the respective investigators.
sections.conclusion: A single infusion of amrecibart or cenvacibart reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism following PICC insertion, suggesting FXI inhibition at the A2 or catalytic domain as a promising prophylactic strategy for contact-mediated thrombosis.

items.title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering.
items.abstract: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor-encapsulated within a GalNAc-lipid nanoparticle-leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

items.title: Single-port Robotic Retroperitoneal Nephroureterectomy with Lower Anterior Access: Surgical Technique, Perioperative and Early Oncological Outcomes from a Multi-institutional Series.

sections.objective: To describe lower anterior access single-port robotic radical nephroureterectomy (LAA-SP RNU), including bladder cuff excision (BCE) and lymph node dissection (LND), without repositioning or redocking.
sections.methods: We present a multicenter retrospective series of 47 patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma who underwent LAA-SP RNU at five referral centers (May 2024-July 2025). A single 4-cm extraperitoneal incision enabled nephroureterectomy, BCE, and selective hilar/pelvic LND without repositioning or redocking. Data were evaluated using descriptive analyses, and pentafecta achievement for the full cohort was estimated through Kaplan-Meier analysis.
sections.conclusion: LAA-SP RNU appears feasible and associated with acceptable perioperative and early oncological outcomes in experienced centers. Comparative prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to establish oncological durability, patient benefit, and cost-effectiveness.
sections.other: Median age of the patients was 72 yr; 95% had high-risk disease. LND was performed in 20 patients (43%). Median docking and operative times were 20 and 220 min, respectively; one procedure was converted to open surgery. Grade ≥3 complications occurred in three patients (6%); median hospital stay was 5 d. Pathology showed pT2 and pT3 disease in 15% and 36%, respectively. At median follow-up of 12.3 mo, seven patients (14.9%) experienced recurrence, including five intravesical recurrences; two died from metastatic disease. The 12-mo Kaplan-Meier estimate of pentafecta achievement was 76.7% (95% confidence interval, 62.8-90.5%). This study is limited by potential referral-center and patient-selection bias, heterogeneity in LND and postoperative management, limited follow-up, and the absence of cost-effectiveness data.

items.title: A 3D Deep Learning Model for Assessing Concomitant Pulmonary Embolism Risk by Integrating Clinical and Computed Tomography Venography Features in Patients with Lower Extremity Deep Venous Thrombosis.

sections.objective: The aim of this study was to develop and validate a multimodal deep learning (DL) model integrating clinical and computed tomography venography (CTV) features for predicting concomitant acute pulmonary embolism (PE) risk in patients with lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (LEDVT).
sections.methods: This multicentre retrospective study enrolled patients with LEDVT undergoing both computed tomography pulmonary angiography and lower extremity CTV. Centre 1 data were used for model training and internal validation, while data from centres 2 and 3 were used for external testing. Clinical models (logistic regression [LR], random forest [RF], support vector machine [SVM], and XGBoost), 3D DL models (VGG-11, VGG-16, ResNet-18, Res2Net-50, and DenseNet-121), and combined models (LR, RF, SVM, and XGBoost) integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features were developed to select the best performer, which was further benchmarked against validated clinical risk scores (Wells score and modified Geneva score).
sections.results: A total of 348 patients from centre 1 were randomly split into training and internal validation sets, and 127 patients from two independent institutions formed the external testing cohort. The optimal LR clinical, 3D VGG-16 DL, and SVM combined models achieved external testing area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.776, 0.789, and 0.836, respectively. DeLong tests confirmed that the SVM combined model significantly outperformed the LR clinical model and validated clinical scores (all p < .050) on the external testing set, while yielding a comparable AUC to the 3D VGG-16 DL model. Decision curve analysis indicated higher net benefit for the SVM combined model, alongside superior calibration, and positive net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement values.
sections.conclusion: The SVM combined model integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features demonstrated robust performance, offering a promising tool for predicting concomitant acute PE in patients with LEDVT.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ulinastatin in the Treatment of Patients with Sepsis: The ADJUST Trial.

sections.objective: Urinary trypsin inhibitor (ulinastatin, UTI) has shown potential survival benefits in sepsis; however, conclusive clinical evidence is lacking.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adult ICU patients with sepsis meeting Sepsis-3 criteria within 48 hours of admission were randomized (1:1) to receive intravenous UTI (400,000 IU every 8 hours) or placebo, for up to 10 days in addition to standard care. Randomization was stratified by site and septic shock. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included ICU, hospital, and 90-day mortality, and ICU/hospital length of stay.
sections.results: Of 347 patients randomized, 340 (169 UTI, 171 placebo) received intervention and were included in the safety analysis; after 5 post-intervention withdrawals, 335 (165 UTI, 170 placebo) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. At 28 days, death had occurred in 39 of 165 patients (23.6%) in the UTI group and in 39 of 170 patients (22.9%) in the placebo group (absolute difference, 0.7% [95% CI -8.4% to 9.7%]; P = .98; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.61, P = .90). Secondary outcomes were similar in the two groups. Adverse events occurred in 56.8% (96/169) of UTI and 42.7% (73/171) of placebo patients (absolute difference 14.1%, 95% CI 3.6%-24.6%; P = 0.009).
sections.conclusion: In patients with sepsis, adjunctive UTI did not reduce mortality compared with placebo. Routine use of UTI for sepsis is not supported by these findings.
sections.other: In patients with sepsis, does adjunctive ulinastatin, compared with placebo, reduce 28-day all-cause mortality?

items.title: Eyelid injury and associations with visual outcomes and globe removal after open globe injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Eyelid injury is identifiable at presentation, but its relationship with visual prognosis and globe survival has not been systematically synthesized. This prospectively registered systematic review and meta-analysis (CRD420261441414) evaluated the association between eyelid injury and visual or globe survival outcomes among patients with open globe injury (OGI).MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through February 21, 2026. Studies reporting visual acuity (VA) or globe survival outcomes stratified by eyelid injury status were included. Eyelid injury encompassed eyelid laceration, lid involvement, eyelid wound, or traumatic involvement as reported by study authors. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E, and certainty using GRADE. Random-effects models generated pooled odds ratios (ORs), with heterogeneity quantified using I². Twenty-one observational studies were included; 14 contributed to quantitative synthesis. Eyelid injury was associated with higher odds of VA worse than 20/200 (OR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.20-2.50; p = 0.0036; I²=0.0%), hand motion or worse (OR, 4.99; 95% CI, 2.04-12.21; p = 0.0004; I²=49.7%), no light perception or worse (OR, 3.04; 95% CI, 2.05-4.51; p < 0.0001; I²=0.0%), and globe removal (OR, 4.22; 95% CI, 1.73-10.34; p = 0.0016; I²=53.0%). The association with VA worse than 20/400 was directionally similar but not significant (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.81-1.87; p = 0.3362; I²=0.0%). Low to very-low certainty evidence suggests that eyelid injury is associated with worse visual outcomes and increased odds of globe removal after OGI. Because the pooled estimates are based on crude, unadjusted comparisons, eyelid injury may reflect established markers of injury severity rather than provide independent prognostic information.

items.title: Successful Management of Infective Native Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Associated With Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis in a 77-year-Old Man.
items.abstract: BackgroundInfected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAAA) is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by rapid progression and high mortality.Case SummaryWe report a 77-year-old male with a history of arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and stage IVB hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma, presenting with lumbar pain and mild inflammatory activation, including leukocytes 8.8 ×10³/µL and C-reactive protein 3.6 mg/dL (normal <0.50 mg/dL). Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 50-mm infrarenal aneurysm, with periaortic inflammatory changes and a periaortic hematoma. A multidisciplinary decision, made 3 hours after admission, favored urgent open surgical repair with resection and in situ reconstruction. Midline laparotomy with debridement and resection of the affected aorta was performed; in situ reconstruction was carried out using a rifampicin soaked bifurcated Dacron graft covered with bovine pericardium with anastomoses to healthy aortic and iliac segments. Intraoperative cultures identified Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis, rare pathogens in this context. Targeted therapy included intravenous ceftriaxone during hospitalization, followed by oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and doxycycline for seven weeks. Histopathology confirmed chronic granulomatous abscessed inflammation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 17. At six months, follow-up imaging demonstrated a patent reconstruction without signs of persistent infection.ConclusionThese findings highlight the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and coordinated multidisciplinary management in achieving optimal outcomes in INAAA, particularly when atypical microorganisms complicate diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making.

items.title: Community health worker-led home blood pressure monitoring in rural sub-Saharan Africa: a diagnostic accuracy study.

sections.objective: Home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) coordinated by community health workers (CHWs) is a potential strategy to improve hypertension detection in sub-Saharan Africa, yet data on its diagnostic performance in this setting are scarce. We aimed to determine the diagnostic accuracy of CHW-coordinated HBPM in Kenya and The Gambia using daytime ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) as the reference standard.
sections.methods: In this cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study, we recruited a random sample of representative age-stratified individuals aged 30 years or older from the general population of two health and demographic surveillance systems in Kilifi, Kenya, and Kiang West, The Gambia. We used the latest enumeration lists of the two health and demographic surveillance systems as sampling frames and performed computer-generated random sampling within five predefined age strata (30-39 years, 40-49 years, 50-59 years, 60-69 years, and ≥70 years). Pregnant women were excluded, and participants were eligible to participate irrespective of previous hypertension status. CHWs trained and provided participants with HBPM devices for self-measurement of blood pressure twice a day, for a minimum of 3 days and a maximum of 7 days. For the reference standard measurement, an ABPM device was fitted by CHWs, and ambulatory blood pressure was measured every 15 min during the day and 30 min at night. We used blood pressure cutoffs derived from the European Society of Hypertension to determine the age-standardised measures of accuracy (sensitivities, specificities, positive predictive values [PPVs] and negative predictive values [NPVs], positive likelihood ratios [LR+] and negative likelihood ratios [LR-] and area under receiver operating characteristic curves) of HBPM among participants who had valid HBPM and ABPM measurements.
sections.results: Between Aug 18, 2023, and Dec 13, 2024, from 1452 eligible participants, we included 1279 participants with valid HBPM and ABPM measurements (696 in Kenya and 583 in The Gambia). In 1279 participants, the median age was 54 years (IQR 43-66), 805 (62·9%) were women, and 474 (37·1%) were men. The age-standardised prevalence of hypertension on daytime ABPM was 23·1% (95% CI 19·9-26·2) in Kenya and 27·1% (23·6-30·6) in The Gambia while the respective prevalences on HBPM were 32·5% (29·1-35·8) and 31·2% (27·5-34·9). The age-standardised sensitivities and specificities of HBPM were 82·6% (76·2-89·0) and 82·4% (79·0-85·7) in Kenya and 68·7% (61·3-76·1) and 83·5% (79·7-87·2) in The Gambia. The age-standardised PPVs and NPVs were 58·6% (52·0-65·2) and 94·0% (91·6-96·4) in Kenya and 59·9% (52·5-67·2) and 88·1% (84·8-91·4) in The Gambia, respectively. The age-standardised LR+ and LR- were 4·68 (3·67-5·69) and 0·21 (0·13-0·29) in Kenya and 4·15 (3·09-5·21) and 0·37 (0·28-0·46) in The Gambia, respectively. In both countries, the area under receiver operating characteristic curve for HBPM was above 75%.
sections.conclusion: HBPM showed moderate-to-high sensitivity and high specificity for detecting hypertension in two rural sub-Saharan African communities. HBPM represents a promising alternative for increasing hypertension awareness in rural sub-Saharan Africa.

items.title: Thoracic epidural versus paravertebral blockade for reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain (TOPIC-2): open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of paravertebral blockade versus thoracic epidural during the perioperative period in reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain.
sections.methods: Open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Adult patients undergoing thoracotomy randomised (1:1) to either paravertebral blockade or thoracic epidural using a web based service between January 2019 and September 2023. Participants in the paravertebral group received three single-shot paravertebral injections of local anaesthetic before incision followed by placement of a paravertebral catheter. Participants in the epidural group had a thoracic epidural catheter placed and loaded with local anaesthetic before incision.
sections.results: 770 patients were enrolled, of which 428 (56%) were male (mean (standard deviation, SD) age 66.6 (11.0) years). After 33 exclusions of patients after randomisation who did not proceed to thoracotomy, 737 remained in the modified intention-to-treat population (364 in the paravertebral group, 373 in the epidural group). Six months after randomisation, 59 (22%) of 272 participants in the paravertebral group and 47 (16%) of 292 participants in the epidural group developed chronic post-thoracotomy pain (adjusted risk ratio 1.32 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93 to 1.86), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI -0.01 to 0.11), P=0.12). During the acute phase, worst and average pain was greater on day 1 with paravertebral blockade (adjusted mean difference 7.7 mm (95% CI 2.8 to 12.5 mm) and 7.0 mm (95% CI 2.7 to 11.2 mm), respectively), but no different on days 2-3. Hypotension was less common in the paravertebral group than the epidural group (12% v 18%, respectively, adjusted risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.94), adjusted risk difference -0.06 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.01)), as was pruritis (4% v 12%, adjusted risk ratio 0.37 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.64), adjusted risk difference -0.07 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03)), although more participants in this group experienced urinary retention (12% v 6%, adjusted risk ratio 2.21 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.61), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09)), complications were similar otherwise.
sections.conclusion: Paravertebral blockade did not reduce chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six month follow-up compared to thoracic epidural. Thoracic epidural provided marginally better acute pain relief one day after the operation, but showed no difference thereafter. Postoperative complications were comparable between groups. The findings support the ongoing use of both techniques.
sections.other: 15 thoracic centres in the UK. The primary outcome was incidence of chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six months after randomisation, defined as a 100 mm visual analogue score greater than or equal to 40 mm (indicating moderate pain) when considering worst chest pain over the past week. Secondary outcomes included acute pain (visual analogue score of 100 mm) and complications.

items.title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch.
items.abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

items.title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China.
items.abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

items.title: Eating disorders.
items.abstract: The eating and feeding disorders are serious psychiatric disorders at the mind-body interface, often with an exceptionally high burden for affected individuals, their families and supporters, and wider society. In anorexia nervosa, high acute medical risk and patients' ambivalence about treatment can make a challenging combination that can impede engagement. First-line treatments for eating disorders are mainly psychological, with medications playing an adjunctive role. Novel biological and technology-based interventions are only slowly emerging. Compared with other psychiatric disorders, research into these disorders is seriously underfunded. Many uncertainties regarding their aetiology, maintenance, and treatment remain. Controversies mainly concern the treatment and care of those with the most severe and longstanding forms of illness. Advances in knowledge are most likely to arise from longitudinal studies combining multimodal assessments, using big data to develop better mechanistic understanding, and greater use of flexible trial designs to allow development of more personalised and precise interventions.

items.title: Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke - New Directions.
items.abstract: In the past 5 years, substantial changes have been made in the use of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Integrating IVT with endovascular thrombectomy, which improves outcomes in patients with stroke due to large cerebral vessel occlusion, has been a particular challenge. This review discusses the underlying vascular targets for IVT and thrombectomy, the increasing use of tenecteplase instead of alteplase, broadening indications for the use of IVT, and ancillary drugs and dosing methods that may augment the success of IVT.

items.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.

sections.objective: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis.
sections.methods: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing.
sections.results: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

items.title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy.

sections.objective: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL.
sections.methods: In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria.
sections.results: A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups.
sections.conclusion: Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

items.title: Retatrutide, a Triple Hormone Receptor Agonist, for Treatment of Obesity.

sections.objective: Retatrutide is a triple-receptor agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, and glucagon receptors.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, randomized, double-blind trial, we assigned adults with obesity without diabetes to receive a once-weekly subcutaneous injection of retatrutide (at a dose of 4 mg, 9 mg, or 12 mg) or placebo for 80 weeks. Primary outcomes (evaluated in the 9-mg and 12-mg groups each vs. placebo) were the percent change in body weight and the change in the WOMAC pain score (ranging from 1 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) in the subgroup of 574 participants with knee osteoarthritis and the change in the apnea-hypopnea index in the 243 participants with obstructive sleep apnea. For weight-related end points, intercurrent events were handled by a treatment-regimen estimand (intention-to-treat [ITT]). For end points in participants with knee osteoarthritis or obstructive sleep apnea, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure; ITT results are also reported.
sections.results: A total of 2339 participants underwent randomization. The mean percent change in body weight in the retatrutide groups was -17.6% (4-mg dose), -23.7% (9-mg dose), and -25.0% (12-mg dose) versus -3.9% in the placebo group (differences, -19.8 and -21.0 percentage points, respectively; P<0.001 for both comparisons). Among the participants with knee osteoarthritis, the corresponding changes in the pain score in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid estimand were -3.2, -3.5, and -3.6 versus -1.9 with placebo (differences, -1.6 and -1.8 points; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -3.4, -3.9, and -4.1 versus -2.5 with placebo (differences, -1.4 and -1.6 points; both P<0.001). Among the participants with obstructive sleep apnea, the corresponding changes in events per hour in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid-treatment estimand were -22.9, -34.3, and -31.7 versus -9.9 (differences, -24.4 and -21.9; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -22.8, -34.3, and -32.1 versus -9.6 (differences, -24.7 and -22.5; both P<0.001). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
sections.conclusion: In adults with obesity, retatrutide resulted in significant weight reduction, reduced pain in participants with knee osteoarthritis, and reduced apnea-hypopnea events in participants with obstructive sleep apnea. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05929066.).

items.title: Targeted Use of Computed Tomographic Coronary Angiography in Acute Chest Pain.

sections.objective: Many patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome in whom myocardial infarction has been ruled out in the emergency department remain at risk for cardiovascular events. Whether further investigation reduces this risk is unknown.
sections.methods: In a multicenter, randomized, controlled trial, patients who presented to an emergency department in 14 hospitals across the United Kingdom were enrolled if myocardial infarction had been ruled out and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin testing indicated an intermediate risk of a cardiovascular event (maximum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I or T concentration, >5 ng per liter). Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either outpatient computed tomographic (CT) coronary angiography-guided care or standard care. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction or death from a cardiac cause.
sections.results: From September 18, 2019, to May 11, 2023, a total of 3170 participants (median age, 61 years; female sex, 30.2%) were assigned to undergo CT coronary angiography (1587 participants) or receive standard care (1583 participants). At 90 days after randomization, CT coronary angiography had been performed in 1462 participants (92.1%) in the CT coronary angiography group and in 35 participants (2.2%) in the standard-care group. Overall, 7 participants (0.4%) had a CT coronary angiography-related adverse event. After a median of 3.0 years, at which point the number of primary-outcome events in the standard-care group exceeded the prespecified minimum of 97, a primary-outcome event had occurred in 112 participants (7.1%) in the CT coronary angiography group and in 116 (7.3%) in the standard-care group (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% confidence interval, 0.73 to 1.23; P = 0.71).
sections.conclusion: In patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome in whom myocardial infarction had been ruled out, routine CT coronary angiography-guided management did not result in a lower incidence of subsequent myocardial infarction or death from a cardiac cause than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation; TARGET-CTCA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03952351.).

items.title: Prevalence of Silent Atherosclerosis across Adult Life.

sections.objective: Atherosclerosis may begin in early adulthood and remain clinically silent for decades before cardiovascular disease manifests. Although silent atherosclerosis is associated with cardiovascular events and death independent of traditional cardiovascular disease risk factors, its age- and sex-specific prevalence, vascular territory distribution, and plaque volume across adult life remain incompletely defined.
sections.methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study in Denmark and Spain. Adults 18 to 70 years of age without known atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled in five prespecified age strata that included balanced numbers of women and men. Silent atherosclerosis was assessed at baseline with three-dimensional vascular ultrasonography of the carotid and femoral arteries and with coronary computed tomographic angiography.
sections.results: A total of 16,808 adults were enrolled in the study. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 45±12 years, and 51.4% were women. Silent atherosclerosis was present in 57.1% of the participants (95% confidence interval, 56.3 to 58.0). In the youngest age stratum (18 to 29 years), atherosclerosis was present in 8.7% of the men and 6.7% of the women; prevalence increased with age, with a later, steeper midlife rise among women. Among participants in the younger age strata, atherosclerosis was most often peripheral and confined to a single vascular territory; with increasing age, plaque volume increased exponentially and the prevalence of multiarterial involvement became more frequent. Isolated coronary-artery atherosclerosis was uncommon in every age stratum (≤9.3% of men and ≤5.0% of women).
sections.conclusion: This study of silent atherosclerosis showed that the disease was detectable in early adulthood, with age- and sex-associated increases in prevalence across arterial territories and marked increases in plaque volume. (Funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation; REACT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06692127.).

items.title: Seladelpar for alkaline phosphatase normalization in primary biliary cholangitis: The IDEAL phase III randomized controlled trial.

sections.objective: Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) <1.67× the upper limit of normal (ULN) has historically been a treatment goal in primary biliary cholangitis (PBC). However, elevation in ALP below this threshold has been shown to increase the risk of disease progression, especially in patients with additional risk factors. We evaluated the effect of seladelpar, a selective peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta agonist approved for PBC, on ALP normalization when levels are above normal but <1.67× ULN.
sections.methods: In this phase III, double-blind trial, patients receiving ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) or intolerant to UDCA with ALP between 1-1.67× ULN were randomized 2:1 to receive once-daily seladelpar 10 mg or placebo for 12 months. The primary endpoint was ALP normalization defined as a composite of ALP ≤ULN with at least a 15% decrease from baseline at Month 12. Secondary endpoints included ALP change over time.
sections.results: Overall, 96 patients underwent randomization. At Month 12, ALP normalization based on the composite endpoint occurred in a significantly higher proportion of patients receiving seladelpar (75.4%, 49/65) compared with placebo (16.1%, 5/31; stratum-adjusted treatment difference [95% CI]: 61.3% [44.9%, 77.7%], p <0.0001). ALP reduction with seladelpar was observed starting from Month 1 and throughout the treatment period (least squares [LS] mean percent change from baseline at Month 12 was -33.8% for the seladelpar group and -5.4% for the placebo group). Adverse event incidence was similar between seladelpar and placebo groups; serious adverse events occurred in 3.1% and 12.9% of patients, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Seladelpar normalized ALP in a substantial proportion of patients with PBC and ALP levels between 1-1.67× ULN despite UDCA use and was generally safe and well tolerated in this population.
sections.other: Most clinical trials in primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) have enrolled patients with alkaline phosphatase (ALP) ≥1.67× the upper limit of normal (ULN). However, evidence indicates that any ALP elevation reflects disease activity and may increase the risk of serious clinical events, including liver transplantation and death. Interest is growing in normalizing biochemical markers in PBC, particularly for patients with high liver stiffness, advanced disease, younger age at diagnosis, or other high-risk features. This is the first phase III study of second-line treatment in patients with PBC and ALP above normal but <1.67× ULN using seladelpar. Compared with placebo, seladelpar led to ALP normalization (ALP ≤ULN with at least a 15% decrease from baseline) in a significantly higher proportion of patients at Month 12, and was consistently observed across subgroups, including those with features associated with disease progression. No new safety concerns were identified. These findings show that ALP normalization with seladelpar is achievable in patients with PBC and baseline ALP levels between 1-1.67× ULN, which may help guide its clinical use. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06060665.

items.title: Passive Sealing Stent-Grafts for Chimney Endovascular Repair: In Vitro Examination and a Japanese Single-Centre Retrospective Study.

sections.objective: Juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms (JAAAs) present with a short infrarenal neck that does not permit standard endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). The AFX VELA cuff extension with its endoskeletal architecture may reduce type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) through passive sealing. We examined this hypothesis using a double-chimney benchtop model and a clinical cohort treated with VELA-based chimney EVAR (ChEVAR).
sections.methods: A benchtop model compared gutter leakage volumes among VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3 (5 trials per device). A retrospective single-centre cohort (January 2018-April 2024) included consecutive JAAA patients undergoing VELA-based ChEVAR with ≥12-month follow-up. Postoperative computed tomographic (CT) morphometry compared seal-zone geometry across the 3 platforms.
sections.results: In the benchtop model, VELA showed a median gutter leakage of 5.0 mL/min (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-11.0), whereas both comparators exceeded 500 mL/min and were right-censored. In the clinical cohort, 20 patients (55% male; median age 80.0 years) underwent ChEVAR for JAAAs with a median diameter of 53.5 mm and infrarenal neck length of 5.0 mm. Clinically successful sac exclusion was achieved in 19 of 20 patients (95%). Intraoperative TIaEL occurred in 5 patients: 1 major endoleak was sealed with adjunctive gutter coil embolisation, and 4 minor endoleaks resolved spontaneously on the 1-month CT angiogram. Over a median follow-up of 36.5 months, no persistent TIaEL was detected on follow-up imaging, and no chimney stent-graft (SG) occlusion occurred. One patient (5%) required an aortic-related reintervention for a type Ib endoleak. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decreased by ≥20% in 9 patients (45%), and 1 started dialysis at 4 years. On postoperative CT morphometry, relative gutter area was lowest with VELA, intermediate with Endurant II and highest with Excluder C3; circumferential apposition followed the inverse pattern.
sections.conclusion: In the benchtop model, VELA produced consistently lower leakage than both comparators, with concordant CT morphometric evidence consistent with a passive sealing mechanism. In this cohort, VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%) with no persistent TIaEL and no chimney SG occlusion. These findings support the feasibility of VELA-based ChEVAR when FEVAR is unavailable; multicentre prospective validation is required.
sections.other: Persistent type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) is a principal limitation of chimney EVAR (ChEVAR) compared with fenestrated EVAR (FEVAR). We report short-to mid-term outcomes of ChEVAR using the AFX VELA cuff extension, whose endoskeletal architecture is designed to promote passive sealing. Postoperative CT morphometry comparing the 3 devices (VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3) showed a smaller relative gutter area and higher circumferential apposition with VELA, paralleling the benchtop pattern. VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%), without persistent TIaEL detected on follow-up imaging. VELA-based ChEVAR appears feasible when FEVAR is unavailable; however, multicentre validation is required.

items.title: Technical Feasibility and Outcomes of t-Branch Proximal Shortening in Urgent Complex Aortic Repair.

sections.objective: Branched endovascular repair has shown consistently good outcomes, being sometimes the only available endovascular solution for aortic emergencies. However, in cases of limited proximal extension of the disease, such as juxtarenal or pararenal aneurysms, branched endografts usually cover a greater extent of the aorta than needed to establish a seal zone, thus increasing the risk for spinal cord ischemia (SCI) by unnecessarily covering segmental arteries.Our objective is to analyze a series of patients who underwent proximal shortening of an off-the-shelf (OTS) branched endograft to limit aortic coverage and preserve segmental arteries.
sections.methods: Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) with a shortened t-Branch, through the removal of the first stent row, from April 2020 to March 2026.Perioperative technical success and complications were evaluated. Primary endpoints were technical success. Secondary endpoints were 30-day mortality, SCI, assessment of number of saved segmental arteries, and endograft migration at follow-up.
sections.results: Fifteen patients underwent BEVAR with a shortened t-Branch endograft. All were urgencies, 60% being ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs). Thirteen (86%) cases were juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysms, and 3 (20%) had a previous endovascular aortic repair. In all cases, the proximal sealing stent of the t-Branch was removed, whereas in 2 cases, an additional large posterior fenestration at the second sealing stent was created. Technical success was 93%, with 1 severely stenotic renal artery not able to be catheterized and left unbridged. No endograft deployment complication (migration or malrotation) were experienced. There was 1 postoperative mortality in a patient with a ruptured AAA. Major complication rate was 27%, including 2 patients having SCI (one grade 2, one grade 3). A median of 2 segmental arteries were saved through the endograft modification.At a median follow-up of 1 year no endograft migration was observed.
sections.conclusion: In urgent complex aortic repair for circumscribed anatomies such as juxta/pararenal aneurysms, the use of a modified OTS branched endograft proved to be a reproducible and safe technique, allowing the preservation of segmental arteries and possibly affecting favorably the spinal cord ischemic rates.Clinical ImpactOn-table shortening of the t-Branch endograft, optionally creating a big fenestration at the second sealing stent, is a feasible and reproducible option for urgent juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysm repair when custom-made devices are not available. The modification allowed sparing a median of two segmental arteries otherwise covered with a standard t-Branch, which might help mitigating the risk of spinal cord ischemia.

items.title: Vascular surgeons have better limb salvage outcomes than non-vascular surgeons in chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
items.abstract: BackgroundWhile the treatment of peripheral artery disease with lower extremity bypass is performed primarily by board-certified vascular surgeons, a subset of non-vascular surgeons continues performing these cases. We investigated differences in practice patterns and surgical outcomes between vascular and non-vascular surgeons for bypass in patients with claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI).MethodsThe ACS-NSQIP targeted database from 2011 to 2022 was used to select non-emergent claudication and CLTI patients. Propensity matching (3:1) was applied to balance demographics and comorbidities between vascular and non-vascular surgeons. Claudication and CLTI cohorts were analyzed separately. Thirty-day outcomes were examined.ResultsFemoropopliteal bypass was the most common procedure followed by femoral-distal bypass for both vascular and non-vascular surgeons. Vascular surgeons were more likely to perform femoral-distal procedures and use single-segment saphenous vein grafts (SSSV) for both claudication and CLTI. Vascular surgeons were less likely to use other non-SSSV conduits for claudication patients (40.6% vs 54.6%, p < 0.01), but no difference in CLTI (38.9%% vs 40.1%, p = 0.74). There was no significant difference in 30-day mortality/morbidities between surgeons for either claudication or CLTI. However, 30-day major amputation for CLTI was significantly better with vascular surgeons (3.0% vs 7.5%, p < 0.01). In CLTI patients, after correcting for operation type and conduit usage, vascular surgeons continued to be associated with lower major amputation (aOR = 0.46, 95 CI = 0.29-0.72, p < 0.01).ConclusionVascular surgeons have better limb salvage than non-vascular surgeons. This could not be explained by the higher use of SSSV; thus, other factors such as surgical skill may account for better outcomes.

items.title: Three-Year Outcomes of Trabeculotomy vs Combined Trabeculotomy-Trabeculectomy for Primary Congenital Glaucoma.

sections.objective: To determine whether trabeculotomy is noninferior to combined trabeculotomy-trabeculectomy (CTT) for primary congenital glaucoma (PCG) with a horizontal corneal diameter (HCD) of 12-14 mm.
sections.methods: Prospective, randomized, controlled noninferiority trial. Children from birth through 3 years of age with PCG, a HCD of 12 to 14 mm, and no previous intraocular or laser surgery were eligible. Two hundred and forty-eight children were enrolled from January 2015 through April 2021, and the final follow-up was completed in April 2024. One eligible eye per child was randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to trabeculotomy or CTT.
sections.results: Overall, 124 children were assigned to trabeculotomy (mean age, 9.8 months; 76.6% male) and 124 to CTT (mean age, 9.9 months; 68.5% male). In the intention-to-treat population, qualified success at 36 months was achieved in 102 of 124 eyes (82.3%) in the trabeculotomy group and 105 of 124 eyes (84.7%) in the CTT group (risk difference: -2.4%; 95%CI, -11.7 to 6.9; Pnoninferiority= 0.004). Corresponding rates in the per-protocol population were 90.3% and 92.9%, respectively (risk difference -2.6%; 95%CI -10.3 to 4.9; Pnoninferiority< 0.001). Mean IOP reduction was -12.1 mm Hg (95%CI, -12.9 to -11.4) and -13.2 mm Hg (95%CI, -14.0 to -12.4) in the trabeculotomy and CTT groups, respectively (P=0.067). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in other secondary outcomes. Adverse events occurred in 56 children (45.2%) in the trabeculotomy group and 67 (54.0%) in the CTT group (P = 0.162). Hyphema was the most common adverse event in both groups, and most cases resolved spontaneously.
sections.conclusion: Trabeculotomy was noninferior to CTT for qualified surgical success at 36 months in PCG patients with a HCD of 12-14 mm. These findings suggest that trabeculotomy may be an alternative to CTT in this population.
sections.other: The primary outcome was qualified surgical success at 36 months, defined as an intraocular pressure (IOP) of 5 to 21 mmHg with or without glaucoma medications, without vision-threatening complications or additional glaucoma surgery. The noninferiority margin was -15 percentage points. Exploratory secondary outcomes included changes in IOP, ocular morphometric and functional outcomes, and adverse events.

items.title: Systematic overestimation using in silico-driven curation in a population database caused reevaluation of the genetic prevalence of Alport Syndrome.

sections.objective: A landmark study by Gibson and coworkers in 2021 estimated that one in 106 individuals carry a predicted pathogenic COL4A3 or COL4A4 variant, suggesting autosomal dominant Alport syndrome is massively underdiagnosed. However, pathogenicity of all triple-helical Glycine substitutions was inferred using in silico tools, which may overestimate prevalence.
sections.methods: COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 variants were extracted from population database gnomADv4.1.1 (about 800,000 individuals, including UK Biobank) and from a clinical exome cohort of 29,055 patients (Eurofins Biomnis), stratified into a kidney disease group (KIDNEY) of 8663 individuals and 20,392 individuals of a non-kidney control group (NON-KIDNEY). Three curation strategies were compared: a ClinVar-dependent model, an in silico-driven model adapted from Gibson, and an Expert Strategy combining stringent allele frequency thresholds, high-confidence loss-of-function filtering, and with ClinVar validation for missense variants. Estimates were validated against the control group and replicated in the non-UKB Biobank subset.
sections.results: Applied to gnomADv4.1.1, the Gibson methodology yielded one in 221, a 52% reduction from the original one in 106 (gnomADv2). The Expert Strategy estimated one in 283, validated in the NON-KIDNEY group (one in 295; concordance ratio 0.96), whereas Gibson inflated the control rate by 91% (one in 154 vs. one in 295). Glycine substitutions (COL4A3 p.Gly1277Ser odds ratio 0.95; COL4A4 p.Gly999Glu odds ratio 1.01) were misclassified by all in silico tools. Expert Strategy variants were found in one in 44 KIDNEY patients (odds ratio 6.76). Enrichment was unchanged by high-confidence loss-of-function restriction.
sections.conclusion: Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome affects one in 283 individuals, one to two orders of magnitude above classical clinical estimates (one in 5,000 to one in 53,000), confirming underdiagnosis, but substantially lower than the Gibson estimate. These findings argue for downgrading the PM2 rarity criterion in collagenopathies. Systematic COL4A3/COL4A4 screening in chronic kidney disease is justified by a diagnostic yield of one in 44.

items.title: Modified immune cell therapy targets kidney-resident tertiary lymphoid structures and ameliorates murine lupus nephritis.

sections.objective: Modified immune cells (MIC), i.e. mononuclear cells challenged with mitomycin C can induce immunotolerance. MIC treatment has been successful in several animal models of autoimmunity and in clinical trials after solid organ transplantation, but the mechanism for reduced inflammation is not fully understood.
sections.methods: To investigate the efficacy of MIC therapy in lupus nephritis, splenocytes from syngeneic NZB/W F1 (BWF1) donor mice were incubated with mitomycin C, and then into BWF1 recipients at 25 weeks of age. Animals were followed for another five weeks to assess disease progression by histological, flow cytometric, and serological parameters. An in vitro phagocytosis assay was conducted to determine the clearance of MIC from 25 patients with lupus and from matched healthy individuals by autologous macrophages.
sections.results: In BWF1 mice, MIC therapy reduced the clinical burden of lupus nephritis disease progression with lower protein excretion and lower serum creatinine levels in the standard-dose compared to the control group. High-dose MIC therapy during active diseases showed no additional benefit. More than 86% of animals had dense lymphocytic aggregates close to the kidney pelvis. These tertiary lymphoid structures differed between MIC-treated animals and controls, with a loss of organization, loss of separation of B-cell and T-cell areas and disintegration of germinal centers after MIC treatment. In the peripheral blood, MIC-treated animals had higher numbers of CD19+CD5+CD1dhigh regulatory-like B lymphocytes. Although MIC treatment was beneficial, higher dosing offered no additional clinical benefit in mice. Macrophages from the patients with lupus efficiently cleared MIC in vitro, ruling out defective clearance as a limiting factor.
sections.conclusion: Our clinically applicable cell therapy approach has the potential to control lupus nephritis by specifically dampening deleterious autoimmune responses.

items.title: Ontogenically distinct macrophages occupy discrete kidney niches and contribute to monocyte recruitment in experimental crescentic glomerulonephritis.

sections.objective: Crescentic glomerulonephritis (cGN) is characterized by aggressive immune-mediated glomerular injury with prominent macrophage accumulation that correlates with disease severity. However, the distinct contributions of kidney-resident macrophages (KRMs) of different ontogenies remain poorly defined.
sections.methods: To explore this, we used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), reporter-based bone marrow chimeras, timed clodronate liposome treatment, and chemokine blockade to define the spatiotemporal dynamics and functional roles of macrophage populations in nephrotoxic serum nephritis (NTSN), a model of cGN.
sections.results: scRNA-seq of total kidney and CD45+ immune cells revealed that proliferating macrophages and infiltrating monocytes expanded sharply by day five and declined by day ten, indicating that local proliferation, in addition to monocyte recruitment, contributes substantially to early macrophage accumulation in NTSN. Two major KRM subpopulations were distinguished by high Ccr2 or Mrc1 expression, consistent with bone marrow and embryonically seeded, self-renewing KRM population, respectively. In Cx3cr1-GFP recipient mice reconstituted with Ccr2-RFP+ donor bone marrow, embryonic-derived GFP+ KRMs were enriched in the outer medulla and corticomedullary region, whereas donor-derived RFP+ monocytes/macrophages preferentially accumulated in the cortex, including within and around the inflamed glomeruli. A timed clodronate liposome regimen that preferentially reduced recipient-retained GFP+ KRMs decreased the cortical accumulation of RFP+ cells, albuminuria, and histologic kidney injury in NTSN mice. Cell-cell communication analysis identified macrophage-associated CCL12 expression, a murine ortholog of human CCL2, as a candidate mediator of cortical CCR2+ monocyte recruitment. CCL12 neutralization reduced cortical monocyte accumulation and ameliorated kidney damage in NTSN mice.
sections.conclusion: These findings indicate that ontogenically distinct and spatially segregated macrophage populations cooperate during early cGN and support further investigation of the CCR2 axis as a therapeutic target for macrophage-mediated kidney injury in cGN.

items.title: Effect of Electronic Behavioral Nudges on Low-Value Preoperative Testing: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: Robust randomized trials have demonstrated that routine testing before cataract surgery does not improve outcomes; however, despite this evidence and long-standing professional society recommendations discouraging routine testing, preoperative testing remains frequent in real-world practice, with most patients undergoing cataract surgery receiving at least 1 preoperative test. To measure whether electronic health record (EHR)-embedded, behavioral science-informed nudges reduce preoperative testing.
sections.methods: This pragmatic randomized clinical trial was conducted at a large academic health system (UCLA Health) in Los Angeles, California. Physicians performing preoperative evaluations were randomized to 1 of 3 EHR nudge alerts or usual care. All encounters with patients undergoing a preoperative visit with a randomized physician within 30 days of cataract surgery were silently enrolled. Patients were enrolled from June 24, 2021, to April 11, 2023. Data were analyzed from June 2020 (1 year prior to first enrollment) to April 2024 (1 year after last enrollment). The EHR interruptive alerts cited professional society recommendations against routine testing; each emphasized a different potential patient harm, including lack of safety benefit, financial burden, or psychological stress.
sections.results: During the enrollment period, 229 of 776 randomized physicians had 1 or more eligible encounter during which a patient was enrolled. Together, these clinicians had 1045 preoperative encounters during the intervention period with 967 unique patients. Mean (SD) patient age was 72.1 (9.1) years, and 595 encounters (56.9%) were with female patients. Mean (SD) signed preoperative testing rates decreased from 83% (29%) to 79% (31%) in the combined intervention arms vs 84% (30%) to 82% (31%) in the control arm. In mixed-effects models, exposure to any nudge was not associated with a reduction in overall testing (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.68; 95% CI, 0.34-1.34). In prespecified secondary analyses, 16% of orders were cancelled following exposure to a nudge, and the psychological stress nudge was associated with decreases in rates of complete blood cell count (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.75; P = .01) and electrocardiogram orders (aOR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.21-0.83; P = .01) vs control.
sections.conclusion: This randomized clinical trial of EHR nudges did not reach statistical significance on the primary outcome of overall preoperative testing. Secondary outcomes suggest future studies might consider the role of a psychological stress nudge in combination with other behavioral, workflow, and/or payment changes.
sections.other: The primary outcome was the change in the proportion of preoperative cataract surgery encounters with any signed testing order(s) between the 12-month period before the physicians' first encounter (enrollment) and the 12-month postencounter period. Secondary outcomes included order cancellation rates among clinicians exposed to the intervention, separate comparisons of each nudge, and analyses comparing orders for specific categories of tests.

items.title: Potential Disparities in Access to Adult Strabismus Care.

sections.objective: Adult strabismus impacts quality of life through diplopia, eye strain, and psychological burden. Access to care may be limited by various factors, yet disparities in adult strabismus care have not been examined nationally. To evaluate potential disparities in access to adult strabismus care across the US by practice type, insurance status, and county-level socioeconomic characteristics.
sections.methods: This national secret shopper study used standardized telephone calls to US pediatric ophthalmology practices identified through the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus and the American Academy of Ophthalmology that simulated appointment scheduling for an adult patients with strabismus. Of 1064 practices contacted, 1060 were included after excluding 4 clinics with disconnected phone numbers. These data were analyzed from August 2025 to September 2026.
sections.results: Overall, 23.8% (252 of 1060) of practices offered an appointment under at least 1 insurance scenario. Patients using Medicaid had a lower appointment success rate than those with commercial insurance (161 of 648 [24.8%] vs 91 of 194 [46.9%]; difference, -22.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -29.8 to -14.3; P < .001). In multivariable regression, other practice types (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.82; 95% CI, 1.28-2.58; P = .001) and commercial insurance (aOR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.67-3.33; P = .001) had higher appointment success, while majority racial and ethnic minority counties (aOR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.45-0.97; P = .04) and lower median household income counties (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.44-0.93; P = .02) had lower odds. Among practices offering appointments, academic centers had longer wait times than other practices (mean [SD], 95.1 [59.3] days vs 57.0 [54.1] days; 38.1 days difference; 95% CI, 21.2-55.1; P < .001), as did lower-income counties (mean [SD], 78.6 [68.1] days vs 61.3 [52.6] days; -17.4 days difference; 95% CI, -33.3 to -1.4; P = .03).
sections.conclusion: This national secret shopper study identified potential disparities in adult strabismus care access. Commercial insurance and other practice types had higher appointment success, while majority racial and ethnic minority and lower-income counties had reduced access and longer wait times. These findings highlight a potential unmet likely benefit of adult strabismus practitioners and support targeted policy interventions to improve equitable access to care.
sections.other: Practice type (academic vs other), insurance type (Medicaid vs commercial insurance), and county-level characteristics, including race and ethnicity majority, median household income, Area Deprivation Index (ADI), and Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Appointment success (ability to schedule appointment during call) and appointment wait time (days between call date and earliest available appointment).

items.title: Genome-Wide Association Study Meta-Analysis of Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.

sections.objective: The pathophysiology of central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) remains incompletely understood, and there is ongoing debate regarding the origin of primary dysfunction. To elucidate the genetic architecture of CSC and map susceptibility loci to specific ocular cell types and molecular pathways.
sections.methods: This genetic association study was a genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis aggregating data from 5 large biobank cohorts and included 2584 patients with CSC and 1 044 455 control participants of European ancestry. Cohort data were from July 1, 2010, to October 31, 2023; data analysis was performed from Febuary 2024 to January 2026. Post-GWAS functional mapping was performed using mendelian randomization, bayesian colocalization, and single-cell disease relevance scoring across human ocular tissue atlases. The relevance of the genetic findings was demonstrated by building a CSC genetic risk score and applying it to the UK Biobank (UKB).
sections.results: The meta-analysis identified 10 risk loci reaching the genome-wide threshold (P < 5 × 10-8), including 3 novel loci (TGFB1, LINC00551, and LOC105375630) and 7 replicated loci (CFH, GATA5, PREX1, CD46, NOTCH4, PTPRB, and TNFRSF10A). Integrative post-GWAS analysis prioritized 10 genes, including TGFB1, TNFRSF10A, and CFH, as likely causal effectors. Single-cell enrichment mapping revealed that CSC genetic risk is concentrated in scleral tissue (P < .001) and vascular endothelial cells (P < .001). Mendelian randomization pointed to circulating TGFB1 and TNFRSF10A levels as associated with CSC risk. A CSC genetic risk score applied in UKB revealed a higher frequency of CSC-relevant abnormalities on macular optical coherence tomography in participants in the top 1% of polygenic risk (18/109 [16.5%] vs 8/134 [6.0%]; difference, 10.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 2.6-19.1; adjusted odds ratio, 4.05; 95% CI, 1.65-10.87; P = .002).
sections.conclusion: Convergent genetic evidence supports CSC as a primary disorder of the sclera and choroidal vasculature with retinal pigment epithelium changes likely representing a downstream consequence. Integrative post-GWAS analysis pointed to complement regulation (CFH, CD46), vascular integrity and endothelial cell signaling (PTPRB, TNFRSF10A, NOTCH4, PREX1), and scleral extracellular matrix biology (TGFB1) as important in CSC.
sections.other: Identification of risk loci reaching the genome-wide threshold, prioritized putative causal genes, enrichment of genetic risk within specific ocular tissues and cell types, and performance of a GRS in the independent UKB dataset.

items.title: Multivessel Assessment by Angiography-Derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance in Patients With Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.

sections.objective: Current guidelines recommend testing for coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in the left anterior descending coronary artery, and it is unclear whether multivessel assessment can improve the diagnostic yield and prognostic value of CMD. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic implications of multivessel CMD assessment using angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (angio-IMR) in patients with nonobstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD).
sections.methods: Angio-IMR was measured in all 3 major coronary arteries in 439 patients with NOCAD.
